title: I LOVE my 77" Samsung S95F!!!
body:
I found an "Open Box" model at a local BB outlet store. They helped me thoroughly check it out before deciding to definitely buy it, and I got a fantastic value. It was described as being in good condition, but it was actually basically new! 

After owning the S95F for about a month now and customizing a couple of picture modes to my personal liking I am blown away by the picture quality... overall the picture quality is absolutely amazing! The TV has fantastic  contrast, tremendous sharpness, and knock out colors, especially with 4K sources. I have watched several of my favorite 4K/UHD discs/movies through my Oppo player that I thought would really show what this TV is made of and OMG... Top Gun Maverick, Star Trek Into Darkness, Avatar Way of Water, Ready Player One, Mission Impossible Dead Reckoning, Blade Runner 2049, Dune 2, Across the Spiderverse, Monsters Inc, and Coco... I never imagined even these brilliantly filmed movies could ever look sooooo good! 

Of course other sources are at least a slight step down in quality, but the apps I have checked out so far: Netflix, Prime, Disney+, and YouTube look great, and even regular cable looks very good! I don't game through the TV, but I've heard it looks fantastic. 

I run all the audio through my receiver and speaker system, so I can not comment on the TVs built in audio/speaker quality. 

The matte/anti-glare screen is highly effective! After owning a 65" LG B7, which I really liked until it built up some nasty burn in after 6 years, I knew I wanted to seriously consider the matte screen models Samsung offers, because I always disliked the mirror like quality of my old B7 and most contemporary OLED screens. Contrary to some things I have read about this Samsung matte screen doing poorly in bright rooms... I completely disagree! We have several big windows and glass sliders to one side of the TV and multiple very bright LED lights opposite the TV. My old B7 completely reflected (almost like a mirror) all those light sources, but the S95F has zero direct reflections and at the most shows extremely slight glare and only in scenes that are almost completely black/very dark!  

I highly recommend this TV for so many reasons. It's probably not perfect for everyone, especially traditionalists who can not get past the matte screen or for those who must have Dolby Vision, but for many  people I strongly believe this would be a fantastic OLED TV choice!

title: Disappointing Customer Experience
body:
I recently purchased the Samsung 85-inch flagship television through Best Buy at a discounted price and was shocked to discover that the customer experience was substantially different from what a consumer would receive when purchasing at full retail price.

What was not made sufficiently clear during the buying process is that this product was fulfilled through a third-party vendor. Once the purchase was completed, it felt as though Best Buy stepped away from the transaction, leaving me to resolve delivery and service issues on my own.

Unlike similar premium television purchases that often include or offer white-glove delivery and installation options, I was required to seek professional installation independently at an additional cost of approximately $300 to $500. For a television of this size and price point, I believe customers should receive the same level of service regardless of whether the item is purchased at a discount.

To make matters worse, my television arrived damaged out of the box, apparently from the third-party vendor's warehouse. The experience that followed was frustrating, with limited accountability and customer support from Best Buy despite purchasing through their platform.

If you are considering this large flagship TV, I strongly encourage you to investigate who is fulfilling the order, understand the installation requirements, and be prepared for potential additional expenses. The television itself may be excellent, but the purchasing and delivery experience was disappointing.

As a long-time Best Buy customer and technology buyer, I expected a higher level of service and accountability. Unfortunately, this experience fell well short of those expectations.

Signed, A Long-Time Best Buy Customer and Tech Enthusiast

The integration with Google TV is seamless. The interface is intuitive, and navigating through apps and settings is smooth and responsive. Google Assistant is a game-changer, allowing for easy voice commands to search for content, control the TV, or even manage smart home devices. The range of apps available is impressive, and having everything from Netflix to YouTube in one place makes finding something to watch a breeze.

The built-in Chromecast is another fantastic feature, making it simple to cast content from my phone or laptop directly to the TV. The audio quality is also quite good for a TV in this price range, with clear dialogue and decent bass.

One of the best things about this TV is its value for money. TCL has managed to pack in a ton of high-end features at a very reasonable price point. The design is sleek and modern, and the setup process was straightforward, with minimal effort required.

Overall, the TCL Google TV has exceeded my expectations. It’s a perfect blend of quality, functionality, and affordability. I highly recommend it to anyone looking for a new TV.

title: Very good TV, for the most part!
body:
Bought ths TV over Labor Day weekend for a very reasonable price! It was on sale for 129.99, so I got $70 off. Shortly after getting it, home, I unboxed it and attached the stands. That went very easy. Next, I turned on the TV and went through the necessary on-screen setup instructions. This took longer than expected probably because I didn't do it through the Google Home app for the setup process. Once it was all set up, I got all the picture and sound settings, etc the way I wanted them. The picture quality of the set is very good. It also has HDR10 capability! The sound on this TV isn't that bad, but I highly recommend connecting a sound bar for much better quality sound! The Google TV OS is a very fun system to use. Just about everything can be accessed from the Google Home screen. I also like the voice control. Definitely cuts down on pressing buttons many times! Picture quality while streaming apps is generally very good also. 

While I like this set in most ways, I do have a few complaints, although not major ones. The remote control, while fully functional, could use better Identification on the buttons by using actual words for each button's function! Another complaint, hopefully minor, is that the wifi will disconnect periodically. I'm not sure what is causing it, but I have my theories. The TV has done a system update 2 times so far, shortly after updating and restarting the wifi is lost, requiring a manual reconnect. The other possibility is with the gateway or something else. I have had a couple laptops either briefly disconnect or show a weak wifi signal, so the tv my not fully be at fault. The tv and said laptops are both in my upstairs bedroom The gateway is located in my living room on the main floor. In addition, this is an xfinity router, so there are very few user adjustable settings. I can't even choose which wifi band I connect dual band wifi devices to. The router chooses the band! This router is 2 1/2+ years old, and I've noticed a weaker wifi signal from several devices in my upstairs. When TCL and Google release updates, they should focus on improving existing functionality as well as new features. With that in mind, I think that this has the potential to be an awesome tv, with strong competition to equivalent sets from Samsung and LG!

If you're looking for a TV with very good Picture quality and lots of internet functionality and reasonable price, this will be hard to beat!

title: The best "budget" 32" TV
body:
The 32" TV market is limited, as in this size range most TV's are just HD (1,280 x 720 pixels).  This is one of two TV's in the sub-$200 range that is FHD (1920 x 1080).  There are a couple of FHD and 4K offerings in the $400 range, but for a budget bedroom TV, this one is probably the best you can buy right now.  32" works fine for watching TV in a bed from a TV on a nearby desk or dresser, although if you have the space, a 43" class TV would be better.
The "Google TV" OS is comparable to Fire TV--it's easy to navigate, and in this TV, it is fairly fast.  It's the latest version of Android TV--it does a good job and has all the apps you would ever need.
The screen looks washed out when viewed from a high angle, but when viewed straight on it is very nice, with vivid, accurate colors.  Once you are in bed watching at the right angle, it is a very nice looking TV.  Horizontal viewing angle is good--it's just the extreme vertical angles that have a problem at extreme angles.
The TV control software is well thought out and has many features, such as being able to control the super-bright standby LED on the front panel.  It's got Bluetooth audio, which is nice for listening with your mate in bed.
Overall, pleasantly surprised.

title: review for TCL s3 32 inch tv with google setup
body: The TCL TV with Google setup (S3) is okay, but not great for blind users. Many popular streaming apps like Hulu, Netflix, and Disney+ are not fully compatible with TalkBack. title: Samsung s95fAbsolutely the Best TV I've Ever Owned
body:
After spending a lot of time researching premium OLED TVs, I decided on the Samsung S95F 83-inch, and it has exceeded every expectation. The picture quality is simply breathtaking. Blacks are perfectly deep, colors are incredibly vibrant without looking artificial, and the brightness is outstanding—even in a bright room.
Movies in 4K HDR look like you're looking through a window rather than at a TV. Gaming on my PS5 is equally impressive with smooth 120 Hz gameplay, VRR, and extremely low input lag. Every game feels more immersive.
I paired it with a Samsung Q990H soundbar, and together they create a true home theater experience. Dolby Atmos movies and games sound incredible, and the combination of amazing picture and powerful audio is hard to beat.
The anti-glare screen is another feature I really appreciate because it does an excellent job reducing reflections during the day without hurting picture quality.
The Tizen smart platform is fast and responsive, and setup was straightforward. The build quality is premium, and the ultra-thin design looks fantastic mounted on the wall.
This TV isn't inexpensive, but if you're looking for the best viewing experience available, it's worth every penny. I would buy it again without hesitation.
Pros:
Stunning OLED picture quality
Incredible brightness and HDR performance
Excellent for movies, sports, and PS5 gaming
Premium design and build quality
Outstanding anti-glare screen

The QLED technology really makes a difference; every scene looks vibrant and detailed, whether I’m watching sports, movies, or gaming. The contrast and color accuracy are out of this world.

title: Exchanged One Lemon for Another
body: I purchased this TV through Costco at a pretty reasonable price, the Costco logistics and delivery were prompt and provided excellent service. The TV itself is literally unusable. The first one that was delivered had a faulty backlight panel, so the picture effectively could not be viewed. There was an image so faint that my iPhone camera could not detect that there was a QR code on the screen and I could only see it with my eyes if looking at the exact right angle a few inches from the screen under specific lighting conditions. I initiated an exchange for this item thinking it happened to be a one-off manufacturing defect and the TV would work fine otherwise. When the replacement arrived, I got it setup and my family sat down to watch a movie streaming through our Apple TV. About 20 minutes into the movie, the screen went black. The backlight panel is clearly still working on the replacement and with all external devices disconnected there is still no picture at all. The TV makes startup sounds and menu beeps when using the remote to try to navigate, but nothing is displayed on the screen, just black that’s bright enough to tell that the backlight is on, but the menus are not visible even though it’s clearly responding to remote input based on audio feedback. I can even get the distinctive beeps of navigating my Apple TV menus while the screen is black if using the Apple TV remote. After spending entirely too long attempting to troubleshoot (power cycling, unplugging the power cord from the wall, pressing the physical power button for ten seconds to try to clear the RAM while unplugged, and finally attempting to use AI to give me the button sequence on the remote to do a factory reset blind) I’m giving up on this model. Now that I’ve already exchanged this product once, I’ll need to contact Costco customer service to see if I can get a refund or credit so I can replace it with a TV from a different manufacturer. Fool me once, Samsung. After many years of using Samsung products, never again.

title: Worst. TV. Ever.
body:
We purchased this from Costco on 4/22/26, returned it 4/27/26. Set-up seemed needlessly complex – QR code this, QR code that. The first thing we noticed was how slow apps were to load and to open. The second was the color. A program would open dim, and then get brighter. The very next scene would again start dim, and then get brighter and so on, throughout the whole program, which is difficult on the eyes and can cause headaches. This occurred on everything we tried to watch, even live newscasts, across each app we loaded. Third, since we are seniors with hearing loss, we rely on captions. This TV had terrible captions. Either they were tiny, unreadable, and off to one side, or if they had 2 or more lines they would appear at the bottom, but only the first line was visible. We could not get normal white on black captions like any other TV. When we tried to adjust the caption position in the settings menu, we got a message saying “This function is not available.” Adjusting captions from within a program also would not work, because the TV’s captioning would override the program’s captioning. Closed captioning technology has been mandated on TVs sold in the US since 1998.  There is no reason a TV manufactured in 2025 and sold in the US should not have usable captioning. Fourth, volume control on the remote had only two options: very low or mute. When we went into the settings menu and tried to adjust the volume there, we again got a message that “This function is not available.” Fifth, one of the main apps I watch is Hallmark+. The app loaded but would not open, saying it needed to be updated. Of course we couldn’t get into it to update it. Updating the TV’s system settings – which we did twice – did not help. This TV almost seemed like it was in beta and not ready for prime time, something we certainly did not expect from a well-known brand like Samsung.

After returning this Samsung TV to Costco, we bought a 55” Roku Plus 4K Mini-LED TV from another retailer (Costco doesn’t sell this model). It was a breeze to set up: printed instructions, no QR codes, and set-up was completed in minutes. Apps loaded and opened quickly. Color is clear, bright, and consistent. Volume can be adjusted with the remote.  Captions can be adjusted from the settings or for individual programs, and look the same on every app we loaded. And the Hallmark+ app opened seamlessly. All at a price lower than the Samsung TV. We would not recommend that Samsung model to anyone.

title: Read my review for accessibility tips
body:
So far so good, with a couple of reservations.   If you don’t have special needs, this TV sets up easily and has a very good picture.  If you have special needs, such as senior with a visual impairment that wants sports and ESPN, the remote is very difficult to use:  small, gray on gray keys, lots of keys, no back light, Alexa voice button in the middle of lots of buttons, etc.   Here is your cheat sheet for free.  

You will likely need a big button remote of some sort.  The one we bought said Hisense compatible.  It wasn’t until I coded it for a Fire TV instead of a Hisense TV.  This is how my visually impaired loved one turns the tv on, mutes the commercials and adjusts volume.

We mostly use YouTube TV for access to local news, CNN and ESPN.  My spouse would be lost without this capability.  However, YouTube TV using Alexa voice control to change channels does not seem to work with the Hisense Fire TV operating system that ships with this TV.  After much finagling, I decided to move the old Fire TV fire stick from our old the tv to this one, and ta da, voice control via any Alexa or echo device on the network will change channels if you phrase it properly.  However this Firestick is not 4k, so the picture quality through it is less.  I’ve ordered a newer 4k (not max) Fire stick for better performance.  We shall see because I have seen some nattering about problems with newer Firesticks and voice control of YouTube TV.  

Note, if there is a power blip, you will become the on-site tech for resolving problems with this set up.  I have no idea how someone else makes this work.  

It’s a pity there aren’t better options for people with visual impairments, Parkinson’s disease which affects movement or cognitive decline.  TV should be accessible to everyone.

The main thing I like in this TV is the switch from Roku to Google, bc Roku interface is just the worst thing in the world, and bc I've been using Google products for over three decades now the interface on the Q77K is pretty intuitive. I installed some apps that take away all the dumb ads and have taken the time to customize what I want and really dialed things in picture-wise, so I honestly have zero complaints about the TV, esp at this price.

title: DO NOT BUY THIS (this is your warning)
body:
DO NOT PURCHASE THIS. Sure, I recognize that some TVs may be defective out of the box. Especially at this price point, it seems like it’s just the nature of the beast. But man, this was frustrating. Right out the gate this thing would crash and black out randomly: adjust volume, switch HDMI inputs, pause Netflix, go to Home menu. And then when trying to restart, it continued to crash before rebooting, an awful loop of turning on over and over only to crash for anywhere from 5-20 minutes at a time. And this was fresh out the box.

Today was day 10. And now for whatever reason, the TV simply will not power on at all anymore. It’s just dead. I’m fairly savvy when it comes to electronics. I troubleshooted myself, with AI, and even spent over an hour with TCL Tech Support, and the resolve was to just return and replace it.

Well, up until today, I thought maybe mine was just defective and a replacement would be fine. And that still could be the case, maybe a replacement WOULD resolve the issues. 

But just the principle of purchasing a NEW TV, only for it to DIE after 10 DAYS is unacceptable. I’m returning this after only 10 days of use and ordered an equivalent from a different manufacturer through Costco for a little extra money. Fingers crossed this other brand isn’t making the same mistakes as TCL.

Seriously. If you’ve read this far and you’re interested in a new TV and this sounds flashy and reasonably priced, be prepared for a lemon. I sure wasn’t. Spend the little extra and avoid TCL. Probably a good reason why I’d never heard of it until I started shopping around for a TV.

title: Great Experience and quality
body:
I'm not sure what some of the 1-star reviewers are talking about.  The picture is AWESOME for the price.  The setup was super-easy and relatively fast.  I was expecting torture authenticating my accounts on a new device.  It was literally about 60 - 90 seconds per app (Youtube TV, Amazon Prime, Disney, Hulu, HBO, Netflix)  Basically you install the app on the TV and open the app on your phone and put in the code, much better experience than typing in passwords and usernames.

title: Only good for YouTube streaming subscribers
body:
This is a so-called smart TV, but it's only smart if you are a Google/YouTube fan. I have Xfinity Streaming service, and when you try to download this app it comes up empty, meaning Google wants you to buy their streaming service which is YouTube. The only way I could make things work was to buy a Roku stick and navigate the apps I want, including Xfinity Stream.
The TV itself is ok for the price, but Costco should tell its customers about the extra cost you have to incur if you want a streaming service for typical channels other than YouTube. It does load the apps for Prime, AppleTV, and Netflix, but those apps only deliver their own content, not other channels you get from a mainstreaming service like Xfinity.

body: I have opened it from the Box and unfortunately, it did not fit in my CRV so hire a truck to deliver and after installation its malfunctioning. There are lines in screen and also vertical colors are coming. Costco asked to return on store. Very Very bad experience.

title: Low/Mid tier TV
body:
Before buying this TV I did some research on QLED vs OLED vs All these other type of panel technologies. So here is my review after mounting, modifying settigns, and using this TV.

Pros: Color looks great, if your kids watch cartoons or anime this is the best bang for the buck. Fast refresh rate really makes a difference. Game consoles take advantage of the gaming settings.

Cons: You will need to set up multiple picture settings. Modified movie mode and motion blur to help with movies. The sound is also on the  low end, a sound bar or dedicated HT setup enhances the experience. The UI is super choppy...if you have an apple TV or Chrome cast/ Fire TV/ Roku that's the best route.

title: Good image - terrible interface
body: So if you need the "smart" functions, look elsewhere. These TVs have several problems with their network stacks that are related to the Google OS you are forced to use. Ethernet connection drops and wireless has never worked well even after setting a static IP address and DNS server. Google insists on hard-coding their DNS server into the stack so . . . if you are concerned about privacy and/or network security, you will want to block this traffic which may then cause other problems. In short, buy an Apple TV or some other dedicated streaming device and forget the "smart" garbage. If you do that, this TV delivers a pretty good image for the money.

title: Absolute 5-star TV, esp at the price point
body:
I have no idea what all the bad reviews for this TV are coming from, but it leads me to believe the level of possibilities with it are more than likely far beyond the capability of the average person buying it. I got the 65" model for less than $400 and if you know anything about the color wheel/coloring it's actually really easy to dial this TV in on almost every mode, especially Filmmaker Mode. All my PS5 games look great, Blu-Rays look spectacular and I've even been a little surprised by the sound. And don't get me wrong, the sound is nothing special from the TV itself, it's just more than I was expecting. 

The main thing I like in this TV is the switch from Roku to Google, bc Roku interface is just the worst thing in the world, and bc I've been using Google products for over three decades now the interface on the Q77K is pretty intuitive. I installed some apps that take away all the dumb ads and have taken the time to customize what I want and really dialed things in picture-wise, so I honestly have zero complaints about the TV, esp at this price. 

Throw in the fact that the screens on all the models at Costco get the special screen on there + 5 years coverage through All-State then I have no idea how anyone could complain about this TV. 

Last thing I'll say - all of you people who leave one and two start reviews bc the TV was damaged upon delivery, that's NOT WHAT REVIEWS FOR THIS TV ARE FOR. That's a knock on the delivery, NOT the TV. Use your brain for something other than a hat rack.

title: Warranty with TCL is useless!!!
body:
This TV is a replacement for one bought last November.  We don't watch often, so in July we contacted TCL for warranty support of a defect noticed immediately but deferred correcting. title: Recommend Staying Away from all TCL products
body:
Purchased this 55” TCL Q77K series TV in December 2025. In June 2026 the screen went black while the audio remained. 

A TCL tech rep walked me through some troubleshooting which did not correct the problem At their request, I supplied a video showing what happens when you turn it on, a photo of the serial tag on the TV and all my Costco purchase info. 

After two tries, they found a local tech who they mailed replacement parts to, who came to my home and install them. He came, installed them and the repair failed. I had a defective tv. 

To get either a new tv or full refund, TCL asked again for the same purchase documentation that was previously provided. 

Finally, after one month, I demanded and was reluctantly given a full refund. 

Their customer service process is flawed and unresponsive.  Not sure they want satisfied customers. They didn’t act like it. 

It’s not what I expected from a Costco supplier. 

I highly advise against purchasing this product or anything from TCL.

title: Bad picture until a couple of setting changes.
body:
85"Q77K, Looked awesome at Costco. At home it looked bad in every way, lacking detail, sharpness, washed out picture and blurry movement. We use a Roku 4k stick. 

Super dissapointed but decided to see if menu changes could make a difference. Oh boy did it! TV looks awesome now. 

In a nutshell, In the Display menu, scroll down to "Automatic Content Recognition" and turn that on. 
In the sub menu "Clarity", turn on "Super resolution". 

Next adjust the Brightness, contrast, etc... to your room.

Boom Bada Bing, great picture!

title: I Didn’t Buy a TV to Play “Hide & Seek”
body:

Trying to close an app is like trying to shut down a Windows 95 computer with a blindfold on. There’s no “close” button, no “quit,” no “exit.” Instead, you have to perform a secret ritual involving multiple menus, a long press, a short press, a prayer, and possibly a blood sacrifice. By the time I finally figured out how to force‑quit Netflix, I felt like I should’ve earned a merit badge.

Apps freeze, lag, and then refuse to die. It’s like the TV is saying, “No, YOU leave.”

There are way better TV’s!!

title: DO NOT BUY THIS (this is your warning)
body:
DO NOT PURCHASE THIS. Sure, I recognize that some TVs may be defective out of the box. Especially at this price point, it seems like it’s just the nature of the beast. But man, this was frustrating. Right out the gate this thing would crash and black out randomly: adjust volume, switch HDMI inputs, pause Netflix, go to Home menu. And then when trying to restart, it continued to crash before rebooting, an awful loop of turning on over and over only to crash for anywhere from 5-20 minutes at a time. And this was fresh out the box.

Today was day 10. And now for whatever reason, the TV simply will not power on at all anymore. It’s just dead. I’m fairly savvy when it comes to electronics. I troubleshooted myself, with AI, and even spent over an hour with TCL Tech Support, and the resolve was to just return and replace it.

Well, up until today, I thought maybe mine was just defective and a replacement would be fine. And that still could be the case, maybe a replacement WOULD resolve the issues. 

But just the principle of purchasing a NEW TV, only for it to DIE after 10 DAYS is unacceptable. I’m returning this after only 10 days of use and ordered an equivalent from a different manufacturer through Costco for a little extra money. Fingers crossed this other brand isn’t making the same mistakes as TCL.

Seriously. If you’ve read this far and you’re interested in a new TV and this sounds flashy and reasonably priced, be prepared for a lemon. I sure wasn’t. Spend the little extra and avoid TCL. Probably a good reason why I’d never heard of it until I started shopping around for a TV.

title: Good image - terrible interface
body: So if you need the "smart" functions, look elsewhere. These TVs have several problems with their network stacks that are related to the Google OS you are forced to use. Ethernet connection drops and wireless has never worked well even after setting a static IP address and DNS server. Google insists on hard-coding their DNS server into the stack so . . . if you are concerned about privacy and/or network security, you will want to block this traffic which may then cause other problems. In short, buy an Apple TV or some other dedicated streaming device and forget the "smart" garbage. If you do that, this TV delivers a pretty good image for the money.

title: Great with Exceptions
body:
Purchased online during the weekend and it was delivered the next Friday. The delivery service showed up an hour early with a one minute prior text alert. I was on my way home and luckily my son was there to let them in. The delivery service left debris on the floor, smeared handprints on the screen and a few other issues I won't detail, just to say the experience lacked attention to detail.

Now for the performance of the QM6K Pro 85". The picture is bright, crisp and no glare even with the blinds fully opened. Some complained about the sound but, I think it is adequate and better than my 12 year old Vizio. 

It looks great until there is fast movement. I couldn't believe how bad the motion blur was out of the box when trying to watch fast moving sports. I literally got dizzy from the tracers. I called TCL customer service and after several minutes of trying to get through the automated system, I was connected to non-US based customer service who was friendly and tried to be helpful but, was really just taking shots in the dark. I later watched some Youtube videos and made several adjustments which helped a lot but,  I still haven't got rid of the motion blur to the point where I'm sure I won't end up returning it. Also, it seems I have to keep changing picture settings depending on the type of programing I am watching at the time. That's already getting old. My 12 year old Vizio has less motion blur and I don't have to mess with the settings every time I turn it on. The jury is still out on this one.

I will try adding a Firestick so see if I can just use the TCL tv as a display only.

author: Gina Jacome

title: Better than expectations. Easy setup
body:
Anyone who has not purchased a new TV in 10 years be warned, these are not TV's. They are internet devices. They must be hooked up to the internet. Samsung TV's are the worst. Read the reviews, people return them because they are so difficult to set up. I did the same last year, and I bought a Sony instead. Sadly, Costco no longer sells 55" Sony sets under $1000. 
The TCL I bought is very good. Setup was easier than expected. They do not make you go thru any hoops if you hook up and external receiving device such as a Roku or Firestick. This is an Android operating system, which is great if you have a Google Smart Home as I do. 
The operating manual is very sparse, I had to do some searches on how to change some settings. They have a QR code to download their app, but I can't figure out how to get my TV on the app because it is not listed. The sound is amazing for a TV. It is not necessary to use my Roku soundbar. The remote works my Google Streamer which is a big plus. They claim the remote is backlit, but it is more like "glow in the dark." It is very dim, and disappointing with all the advances in LED technology that the buttons are very dim. The most important button, the microphone button, doesn't glow at all. 
The picture is very good. The picture  does not change significantly, if at all, from different viewing angles.  I wish the power cord was longer. They recommend only to set it up on a flat surface. I mounted it in on a wall, and the cord just barely covers the distance I need. 
This rivals my 65" Sony which cost a few hundred dollars more. I use this in my bedroom, so I am not too fussy about the picture, but it is very good. Much better than expectations. The 5 year warranty is a big selling point.

title: TV died after a day and a half. What a waste!

title: Great picture and a great value.
body:
We purchased this unit about a month ago. We were hesitant, but trust Costco's return policy. We are amazed by the picture quality. Very easily can say "this is all the TV we could ever need." 

SDR shows look great. Even old content from 2014 - on Comet TV channel looks really great. Sound needs to be played with, but you can dial it in to whatever you prefer. Saw a little judder, but just had to change the settings and it went away. There is literally an adjustment for everything, so you can fine tune whatever you like.

Great picture quality at a bargain - especially if you catch a sale (every 10-14 days)

title: Customer Beware
body: BEWARE! The 1 year manufacturer's warranty on TCL smart TVs puts the purchaser through extensive online verification steps to prove faulty TV issues. All of these steps are requested of the customer through their online TCL Chat page (apparently purchasers don't have an option to have the TV issue looked at in person at any point based upon my experience). I purchased my TCL 75QM6K from Costco.com in September of 2025. It is still under the manufacturer's warranty. In contacting TCL about my screen's recently faded picture and lack of color and brightness about 3 weeks ago, TCL support has required me to send them TV program videos and screen photos illustrating my issue. Although I have forwarded them 5 videos and screen photos at several different requests, as of today 7/28/26 they are still requesting more video. It appears that this large TV manufacturer does not contract out to technicians to assist customers in person even in large metro areas such as Dallas/Fort Worth where I made my online Costco purchase. TERRIBLE customer warranty support from TCL. Luckily I purchased the Costco extended warranty because it appears that TCL is looking for any way they can to deny customer's claims during their warranty period.  Beware of TCL TVs!

Better pictures of the feet that need to be attached would have helped as they are not symmetrical and that was the most difficult part of the setup. The picture is excellent. title: Excellent TV, especially for PC and Mac use
body:
I’m glad I put the brand snobbery aside, because this is a great TV. Google TV is a much more open platform, it feels native, and it gives you a lot more flexibility than some of the other smart TV systems.

I had been anxiously waiting for the next Apple TV to come out, and at this point, I no longer care. The TV itself and the Google interface are that good.

The Mini-LED technology is also ideal if you use the TV with a PC or Mac. The picture is sharp, bright, and works very well as a large computer display.

My only real gripe is that you cannot use wired Ethernet and Wi-Fi at the same time. Google Cast needs the TV to be on Wi-Fi, so you have to choose between the convenience of casting and the benefits of a hardwired connection. The workaround is using another HDMI input from your laptop when you want to play YouTube or other content while keeping the TV hardwired.

Other than that, I’m thrilled with it. Great picture, great platform, and a great value.

title: Happy so far.

title: Very good TV, good price.
body: I bought this for my mother six months ago during the Super Bowl sales.  She recently moved into assisted living and the new geometry of her apartment meant that she couldn't easily see the guide on her 43" TV.  Swapping it for a 65" tv fixed that problem.  It's a very good TV at a good price.  I'm surprised how nice it is compared to my old TCL Roku 55" from 7 years ago.  I'm not a huge fan of the Google TV interface though, so we've paired it with a Tivo Stream 4k for now.  I hope I can get another Google TV box set up with edited buttons on the remote control so she is able to work it as intuitively as she does the Tivo, and her cable TV tivo before.

title: Great Picture Quality, Terrible Quality Control
body:
This TV has great picture quality for the price, with bright colors and deep black levels. This model however suffers from terrible quality control that I want to warn people about before they buy. 

My first unit came with a 2" long "dark smudge" on the top right corner that couldn't be cleaned off. It must have been dust under the screen or a backlight defect. Costco made it easy to "request replacement" online and schedule a delivery of the new tv and pickup of the defective tv. 

When I setup the 2nd TV, I noticed several areas of "dirty screen effect" in the center, top and right side of the tv. The first tv didn't have any noticeable DSE at all. Costco.com only lets you replace an item once, so I'm unable to request another exchange online.

My local warehouse doesn't carry the 55" so I can't just swap it out there. The price has also gone up $100 since the sale ended so I can't just return it and buy another. 

At this point I wouldn't reccomend TCL or the QMK Pro because you will probably end up with a defective one anyway.

title: Great buy at Costco!
body: I was hesitant about purchasing a TV with a technology not known to me as this hybrid QLED and Mini LED together. I have other TLC QLed TV’s in 65” and 55” and in my opinion, the picture on those was flat and al little washed out. Not the case on this one! When watching the on board TV promotional presentation at the Costco warehouse, I was taken aback about the clarity, colors and depth of view on this TV. I know it is a 8K recording and everything in the picture is perfect, but the reproduction of it on that TV was awesome.  I’m replacing a 75” Sony Bravia after 6 years of service as the LED screen went dead, so my standards for picture quality were very high. This TLC 85” hybrid Mini Led-QLed didn’t disappoint. It is bright and colorful. Great definition. I’m using in the vivid picture setting because I like exactly that, a vivid picture. Didn’t have to do any adjustments, I just left it on the factory settings. I’m watching mostly through a Firestick 4K dongle. Netflix picture is amazing, and other shows look great as well. I connected it to my Onkyo home theater receiver (and plugged in all my components there, included the Firestick) and connected the TV out to the TV with only one HDMI cable. I didn’t test the TV sound, even though I imagine it must be pretty good considering the 2 subwoofers in the back of the TV. Everything else are pretty much the standards you will find in most current TV’s. I also like the location of the connection panel, which is easily receable on the side of the TV (even though I had to use a very long HDMI cable because of the size of the TV and the distance to the receiver). Considering a purchase price of $1200 with free delivery and the free additional 3 years of warranty from Allstate added to the 2 years given by Costco (they give an additional 1 year on top of the manufacturer’s warranty), I have 5 years to enjoy this beauty without worrying about paying for repairs if needed (hopefully not!). It’s been only 1 day in service, so cannot tell much more. I’ll update if I have any new comments.

It replaced a Hisense that failed which was a budget TV, this TV is leagues ahead in every way.  65 to 75 is a pretty big jump in comparison.  Wife loves it.  Deep blacks and bright white/colors.  Seems uniform across the entire screen.  The screen is not matte.  As others have stated, I dont know if Costco still has any anti glare with the "Pro" nomenclature. title: Good TV, but not great as upscaling is poor (IMHO)
body:
I have been using this TV for the past week or so and here are my comments on it:
The Good:
 - Colors are very good and seem true to life
 - The local dimming for the backlight seems to work pretty well, blacks can be very "BLACK" making the colors pop
 - Most function except for the up-scaling seem to work well
 - The anti-reflection seems to be effective when viewing straight-on
 - Got a replacement TV in pretty short order as the first one arrive with a cracked screen
- The google interface sync'd immediately to my account remembering all the apps and passwords I had. 
- The lag between what the video shows on the screen and what the sound outputs seems to be okay, not sure at this time if there is any fine tuning adjustments that can be made to get it close to perfect, but so far it is acceptable.
The BAD
 - As mentioned previously, the up-scaling is poor, so bad, that I turned it off as it blended colors together, un-watchable
 - I did not know what to expect from the anti-reflection coating, but when you view the screen from just a few degrees off-axis, there is a lot of reflections that happen,   When you view on-axis, it works great.   Don't know if this is what to expect from all AR coatings, or if it is just a cheap AR coating with limitations on viewing angle.

Misc: I have not used the internal speakers for sound, so I cannot comment on the audio from them (I have a good sound bar attached via the eARC port).    Overall, pretty happy with this purchase.

title: No Complaints
body: I felt compelled to review this TV mainly to counteract the prevalence of overly negative reviews I see on Costco. Many of the negative reviews don't even have anything to do with the actual TV, but are complaining about delivery or something unrelated to the TV. Ugh. Makes shopping for a new TV frustrating, which is the position I was in until a week ago. I had a TCL S535 75" that had a faulty backlight really from the time we purchased in 2021 that got progressively worse. To TCL's credit, they replaced under manufacturer's warranty after we had it almost a year (didn't purchase at Costco). The replacement TV, however quickly developed the same issue. I think we just got unlucky twice because the TV reviewed well at review sites and elsewhere and these 2 TVs had the issue almost from the get go. Anyway after suffering through the replacement TV for 4 years I decided to shop for a new one. At first I was going to avoid TCL because of that experience, but QM6K, QM7K, or QM8K kept showing up on my radar when searching for best bang for buck TVs. I went ahead and settled on QM6K for cost reasons and decided to purchase through Costco for the 5 year protection in case we got unlucky again. It's only been a week, but this TV has exceeded my expectations. The only thing I will say that I do agree with on many of the negative reviews is that the anti reflective surface in my opinion does leave much to be desired. TV is in living room with lots of windows that get very bright when sunny outside and the reflections are very apparent. However, when TV is set to brightest it's able to counteract most of that. I really can't complain for this price point and this TV does handle reflections much better than TV we replaced. I did look at the non-Pro that is the version of QM6K at other stores and that matte finish just seems to keep the TV from looking its best. At night this TV absolutely pops and I'm impressed every time I watch something on it.

title: TCL 75" Class - QM6K Pro Series
body:
This review is for the TCL 75" QM6K.

Purchased on 1/18/26 and delivered on 1/22/26.  All went fine.  
I don't think you can beat the price/performance for this TV.  The picture quality has been excellent.  The TCL CrystGlow HVA (Hyper-Vertical Alignment) panel is a premium, high-contrast display technology designed for 2025 QD-Mini LED TVs like the QM7K/C7K/C9K series. It offers superior contrast (up to 7000:1), faster response times (1ms), and better anti-reflective coating for enhanced image clarity and reduced blooming.  This panel is only offered on the Costco QM6K TV's and I truly believe it makes a huge difference.  I saw an 85" QM6K at another warehouse and it had a matte display and it's nowhere near as bright and colorful.

I watched the 2026 Winter Olympics on Peacock and the 4K content was crystal clear, bright and colorful.  I was amazed!!!!  I could have watched it on my Dish Network satellite feed  I was shocked how much better the Peacock stream was than the Dish feed.

I'm very, very impressed and satisfied with this TV.

title: Massive upgrade over the UH80
body:
We originally purchased the Samsung UH80 and were pretty happy with it, but after upgrading to the Highsense U65 Pro, the difference in picture quality is honestly much bigger than I expected.
We live in a very well-lit apartment, and the anti-glare screen on the U65 Pro has made a massive difference during the daytime. The UH80 would pick up reflections from our windows and lights that could be distracting, whereas the U65 Pro remains extremely watchable even with a lot of light in the room. It makes a bigger difference in everyday viewing than I expected.

The Mini-LED picture is also a huge step up. Blacks are much deeper, contrast is noticeably better, highlights have much more impact, and HDR content looks significantly more impressive. Colors also have more depth and the overall picture just looks much more premium than the UH80. Watching the two side-by-side really makes the difference obvious.

The sound is another huge improvement. The built-in speakers sound substantially fuller and more powerful than the UH80, and the built-in subwoofer is legitimately impressive for a TV. Bass has considerably more impact than I expected from a television without a separate soundbar or subwoofer. Movies and especially action scenes sound fantastic.

One minor issue: getting our Apple TV 4K remote to control the TV volume was a little challenging. The initial HDMI-CEC setup didn't work correctly, and the Apple TV also wouldn't initially learn the Hisense remote's volume commands. After some troubleshooting and changing a few settings, we were eventually able to get the Apple TV remote controlling the TV volume. So it is possible, but it wasn't completely plug-and-play.

The Hisense interface is also a little less intuitive than Samsung's UI. If you are already used to Samsung TVs, there is a bit of a learning curve with some of the menus and settings. That said, the built-in apps work well and are nice to have if you don't already have a streaming device. Personally, I would highly recommend using an Apple TV or another dedicated streaming device as your primary interface if you have one. The Apple TV experience is much more polished and intuitive, and the U65 Pro really shines when you're using it primarily as the display rather than relying on its built-in interface.

Overall, we're extremely happy with the U65 Pro. Coming directly from the Samsung UH80, the improvements in picture quality, daytime viewing, and especially sound are substantial. For a bright apartment where glare is a concern, the anti-glare screen alone is a major upgrade. At the Costco price, this feels like an excellent TV for the money.

title: Hands Down Best Value in a 2026 LED TV Model
body:
I'm my A/V Enthusiast opinion, there is no better value on the market for 2026 model TVs.  Ya, many people are going to give it 5 stars like they would on a new set of tires for their car. If you are coming from a 5+ year old smaller TV, the new TV is fantastic just like the new tires are coming from driving around on worn out tires. This TV for the money actually IS fantastic.  I would only get the TCL QM6K Pro if you are an avid gamer and need the fastest response time possible.

Some technical reviews criticize the pixel response and say fast action is blurry. Virtually no one is going to notice unless they are doing a side by side comparison with a much more expensive TV.  I tested with hockey which I can barely follow the puck when I'm at the arena, tennis, football, F1.  There's no level of blur that I was like "this is unacceptable". In fact like the vast majority of reviewers, watching sports is a pleasure. Is another unit potentially a little more clear, maybe but you're not going to get it for $749 + 5 year warranty. Plus if you really need as much anti-glare/reflection as possible this is the no-brainer budget choice.  Black levels and contrast for the price are incredible. This is the best TV deal I've seen in the past 5 years. No noticeable DRE either on the panel I got. Ya the 1% of the very corner is a little dark but that's normal for a mini-LED and not noticeable in normal viewing.  There is also some barely noticeable darkening on the outer 8% of the screen but I had to look for it. Sit 100 people in front of it, and 99/100 won't even see it. I was expecting less uniformity at this price so I was pleasantly surprised.  

Note that I could care less about Fire TV as I use an ONN Plus Google TV puck so I can just plug that into whatever TV I choose including taking it on vacation. Most people aren't even going to know the best settings to use in the gazillion picture settings this thing has.  Ask AI to help you fine tune it to your liking.

Don't waste your money on a name brand (Sony, Samsung) because of the brand. Do your homework. It's either this or you have to step up to a $2K OLED TV and do you REALLY need the benefits of the OLED TV? Probably not.

I guess I will be a contrarian in reviewing this tv. I received it last Thursday. In deference to the tv, when the delivery folks came I noticed that the tv was placed on the long end in the truck and strapped to the side of the truck. It was not sitting like you would see a tv on the floor at Costco. The delivery truck came from roughly 45 miles away. There was no damage to exterior of the box.

The delivery folks were efficient and had the tv assembled in minutes.
Based on the reviews here and online, I was expecting a really great picture. After owning this tv for a few days, I have found the picture to be dull and lack detail out of the box. The picture is best described as "hazy". I am not sure if I would say if the anti-glare screen is partially the cause. I know that our computer monitors in the house that have the matte screens lack the detail of the glossy screens and it seems to be true of this tv.

Roughly 60% of the screen suffers from Dirty Screen Effect (DSE). Starting from the center of the screen and radiating out about 30% on either side. It shows up most demonstrably when running a DSE test online, and further while watching motion during live tv. Whether this is the result of how the way it was loaded on the truck, or really poor quality control at the factory, it is not acceptable.

If you plan to use a cable box, such as Xfinity or any other cable provider, be prepared for a poor quality picture. I tried a few different HDMI cables including purchasing a brand new HDMI 2.1 cable, all to no avail. My other Samsung TV's in the house show much more clarity and detail running off cable boxes.

Another oddity is, when using an app, using the remote to rewind and then resume play, the picture FREEZES EVERY TIME. The sound continues to work, but the pictures is frozen. I don't know if it's the processor that is causing the issue or not. None of my other four tv's in the house exhibit this behavior.

I was going to see if things would improve over the next few days, but at this time I think it's pointless and I'm just going to have the tv returned. 

I will add that the largest tv we had in the house was a 50". I don't think that the size of this tv has led to the picture degradation. I went to Costco and they did not have this tv on the same feed as all the other tv's in the store. But, the other 75" tv's that were higher priced definitely showed a clearer more defined picture.

One of the biggest surprises for me was the audio. Usually, modern flat-screen TVs have terribly thin audio, forcing you to immediately go out and buy an external setup. Not this one. As for the smart features, the app sync is great. Setup was completely seamless, and logging into all my streaming platforms was quick and painless. The interface is snappy, responsive, and doesn’t suffer from the annoying lag you often get with built-in smart TV software. Everything just works beautifully together.

Another massive pro for this unit is the 120Hz refresh rate. I wanted something that could handle fast motion without blurring, and this TV delivers flawlessly. Watching fast-paced sports is incredibly smooth, and if you are a gamer, the 120Hz makes gameplay feel incredibly fluid and responsive. title: Great TV, Good in a Bright Room
body:
We bought this in July after we moved into a new house. The last TV I bought was a 55” TCL in 2017 or so. The TCL wasn’t a horrible TV, especially for what we paid, but this 77” OLED blows it out of the water. 

We have mixed viewing habits: streaming shows, video games (only single player on PS5 so I can’t attest to the performance of FPS or other competitive games), sports and movies. I am waiting for a sale on soundbars around Black Friday so we have been using the built in speakers. They work well enough but the spoken word is a bit muddled. 

The room it is in gets extremely bright afternoon light from a window on the opposite wall and the screen is bright enough to work well in there. It is actually a bit too bright and I have had to turn it down quite a bit because it was straining our eyes. 

I have yet to have time to sit and enjoy any preseason football this season but I don’t think we will have any issues with the picture once football season starts in a few days. 

The magic remote is pretty cool and quite useful to navigate around such a big screen without clicking directional-buttons a million times. I do wish there were a dedicated mute button. You have to hold down the volume down button for one second and it will mute. If you have the volume up very high it makes for a tedious process to get it down to a low level. 

I hung it in the wall with a low profile Sanus mount I bought at a big box electronics store. LG seems to not have changed the orientation of the back for the last number of generations of this TV so I used the Sanus website height tool to mark out on the wall where we thought our toddler wouldn’t be able to slap it and it still be at a comfortable height. I did notice his little hand print on the screen this evening so that plan wasn’t as successful as I had hoped.

Costco delivery was easy, glad I bought it here!

title: Great Picture but full of AI Software Bloat
body:
This is a fantastic OLED TV. LG makes some of the best OLED panels and this does not disappoint.  I would however strongly recommend NOT connecting this TV to the internet.  The software is full of AI bloat and adware, designed to gather your data and sell you ads.  Use a streaming device such as a Roku, Apple TV or Fire Stick instead. 

LG, like most modern TV manufacturers, is increasingly in the data and advertising business. LG’s webOS platform business surpassed $700million in annual revenue in 2024, driven in part by advertising and content.

If you use the built-in Smart functions (webOS), the TV can gather information about what you’re watching, including content viewed through connected sources, to support personalization and advertising. Compound that with LG’s need to slap “AI” on everything. The TV even has Microsoft Copilot and a chatbot built in.

Bottom line: great panel, great price.  Buy it but never connect it to the internet. Use an external streaming device.  (TV software updates can be done via a USB stick)

title: Read my review for accessibility tips
body:
So far so good, with a couple of reservations.   If you don’t have special needs, this TV sets up easily and has a very good picture.  If you have special needs, such as senior with a visual impairment that wants sports and ESPN, the remote is very difficult to use:  small, gray on gray keys, lots of keys, no back light, Alexa voice button in the middle of lots of buttons, etc.   Here is your cheat sheet for free.  

You will likely need a big button remote of some sort.  The one we bought said Hisense compatible.  It wasn’t until I coded it for a Fire TV instead of a Hisense TV.  This is how my visually impaired loved one turns the tv on, mutes the commercials and adjusts volume.

We mostly use YouTube TV for access to local news, CNN and ESPN.  My spouse would be lost without this capability.  However, YouTube TV using Alexa voice control to change channels does not seem to work with the Hisense Fire TV operating system that ships with this TV.  After much finagling, I decided to move the old Fire TV fire stick from our old the tv to this one, and ta da, voice control via any Alexa or echo device on the network will change channels if you phrase it properly.  However this Firestick is not 4k, so the picture quality through it is less.  I’ve ordered a newer 4k (not max) Fire stick for better performance.  We shall see because I have seen some nattering about problems with newer Firesticks and voice control of YouTube TV.  

Note, if there is a power blip, you will become the on-site tech for resolving problems with this set up.  I have no idea how someone else makes this work.  

It’s a pity there aren’t better options for people with visual impairments, Parkinson’s disease which affects movement or cognitive decline.  TV should be accessible to everyone.

title: Massive upgrade over the UH80
body:
We originally purchased the Samsung UH80 and were pretty happy with it, but after upgrading to the Highsense U65 Pro, the difference in picture quality is honestly much bigger than I expected.
We live in a very well-lit apartment, and the anti-glare screen on the U65 Pro has made a massive difference during the daytime. The UH80 would pick up reflections from our windows and lights that could be distracting, whereas the U65 Pro remains extremely watchable even with a lot of light in the room. It makes a bigger difference in everyday viewing than I expected.

The Mini-LED picture is also a huge step up. Blacks are much deeper, contrast is noticeably better, highlights have much more impact, and HDR content looks significantly more impressive. Colors also have more depth and the overall picture just looks much more premium than the UH80. Watching the two side-by-side really makes the difference obvious.

The sound is another huge improvement. The built-in speakers sound substantially fuller and more powerful than the UH80, and the built-in subwoofer is legitimately impressive for a TV. Bass has considerably more impact than I expected from a television without a separate soundbar or subwoofer. Movies and especially action scenes sound fantastic.

One minor issue: getting our Apple TV 4K remote to control the TV volume was a little challenging. The initial HDMI-CEC setup didn't work correctly, and the Apple TV also wouldn't initially learn the Hisense remote's volume commands. After some troubleshooting and changing a few settings, we were eventually able to get the Apple TV remote controlling the TV volume. So it is possible, but it wasn't completely plug-and-play.

The Hisense interface is also a little less intuitive than Samsung's UI. If you are already used to Samsung TVs, there is a bit of a learning curve with some of the menus and settings. That said, the built-in apps work well and are nice to have if you don't already have a streaming device. Personally, I would highly recommend using an Apple TV or another dedicated streaming device as your primary interface if you have one. The Apple TV experience is much more polished and intuitive, and the U65 Pro really shines when you're using it primarily as the display rather than relying on its built-in interface.

Overall, we're extremely happy with the U65 Pro. Coming directly from the Samsung UH80, the improvements in picture quality, daytime viewing, and especially sound are substantial. For a bright apartment where glare is a concern, the anti-glare screen alone is a major upgrade. At the Costco price, this feels like an excellent TV for the money.

title: Hands Down Best Value in a 2026 LED TV Model
body:
I'm my A/V Enthusiast opinion, there is no better value on the market for 2026 model TVs.  Ya, many people are going to give it 5 stars like they would on a new set of tires for their car. If you are coming from a 5+ year old smaller TV, the new TV is fantastic just like the new tires are coming from driving around on worn out tires. This TV for the money actually IS fantastic.  I would only get the TCL QM6K Pro if you are an avid gamer and need the fastest response time possible.

Some technical reviews criticize the pixel response and say fast action is blurry. Virtually no one is going to notice unless they are doing a side by side comparison with a much more expensive TV.  I tested with hockey which I can barely follow the puck when I'm at the arena, tennis, football, F1.  There's no level of blur that I was like "this is unacceptable". In fact like the vast majority of reviewers, watching sports is a pleasure. Is another unit potentially a little more clear, maybe but you're not going to get it for $749 + 5 year warranty. Plus if you really need as much anti-glare/reflection as possible this is the no-brainer budget choice.  Black levels and contrast for the price are incredible. This is the best TV deal I've seen in the past 5 years. No noticeable DRE either on the panel I got. Ya the 1% of the very corner is a little dark but that's normal for a mini-LED and not noticeable in normal viewing.  There is also some barely noticeable darkening on the outer 8% of the screen but I had to look for it. Sit 100 people in front of it, and 99/100 won't even see it. I was expecting less uniformity at this price so I was pleasantly surprised.  

Note that I could care less about Fire TV as I use an ONN Plus Google TV puck so I can just plug that into whatever TV I choose including taking it on vacation. Most people aren't even going to know the best settings to use in the gazillion picture settings this thing has.  Ask AI to help you fine tune it to your liking.

Don't waste your money on a name brand (Sony, Samsung) because of the brand. Do your homework. It's either this or you have to step up to a $2K OLED TV and do you REALLY need the benefits of the OLED TV? Probably not.

title: You get what you pay for
body:
I guess I will be a contrarian in reviewing this tv. I received it last Thursday. In deference to the tv, when the delivery folks came I noticed that the tv was placed on the long end in the truck and strapped to the side of the truck. It was not sitting like you would see a tv on the floor at Costco. The delivery truck came from roughly 45 miles away. There was no damage to exterior of the box.

The delivery folks were efficient and had the tv assembled in minutes.
Based on the reviews here and online, I was expecting a really great picture. After owning this tv for a few days, I have found the picture to be dull and lack detail out of the box. The picture is best described as "hazy". I am not sure if I would say if the anti-glare screen is partially the cause. I know that our computer monitors in the house that have the matte screens lack the detail of the glossy screens and it seems to be true of this tv.

Roughly 60% of the screen suffers from Dirty Screen Effect (DSE). Starting from the center of the screen and radiating out about 30% on either side. It shows up most demonstrably when running a DSE test online, and further while watching motion during live tv. Whether this is the result of how the way it was loaded on the truck, or really poor quality control at the factory, it is not acceptable.

If you plan to use a cable box, such as Xfinity or any other cable provider, be prepared for a poor quality picture. I tried a few different HDMI cables including purchasing a brand new HDMI 2.1 cable, all to no avail. My other Samsung TV's in the house show much more clarity and detail running off cable boxes.

Another oddity is, when using an app, using the remote to rewind and then resume play, the picture FREEZES EVERY TIME. The sound continues to work, but the pictures is frozen. I don't know if it's the processor that is causing the issue or not. None of my other four tv's in the house exhibit this behavior.

I was going to see if things would improve over the next few days, but at this time I think it's pointless and I'm just going to have the tv returned. 

I will add that the largest tv we had in the house was a 50". I don't think that the size of this tv has led to the picture degradation. I went to Costco and they did not have this tv on the same feed as all the other tv's in the store. But, the other 75" tv's that were higher priced definitely showed a clearer more defined picture.

Another massive pro for this unit is the 120Hz refresh rate. I wanted something that could handle fast motion without blurring, and this TV delivers flawlessly. title: 98” Samsung U9000H — Great value, but calibrate it
body:
Nothing else at 98” comes close on value. ($1499) One tip: turn off the AI picture settings and calibrate it. I switched to Movie mode, Color Tone Warm1, and ran the free AVS HD 709 patterns on YouTube — brightness, contrast, sharpness, black clipping. Thirty minutes, dramatic difference. Sharpness landed at 2, not the 20+ the presets ship with.

After calibration the blacks are close to mini-LED. Running a Roku Ultra and the picture is razor sharp — the upscaling on 720p/1080i sports broadcasts is impressive.

Also turn off Auto HDR Remastering and enable Input Signal Plus on your HDMI port. Spend the half hour calibrating and this punches way above its price. I compared to the Hisense QD7 and this blows that one out of the water for sports and off axis viewing.

title: Big Disappointment!
body:
We've exclusively bought Samsung TV's over the years, many of them, and they've been great, until this one. 

The first problem is the power cord socket on the back is stupidly covered by the wall mount bracket, making installation complicated and difficult, and in our case, wasn't even possible with the included power cord, so we couldn't mount it till we found another power cord that would fit. 

The next problem is the TV is much more complicated, made worse by the new remote which is terrible, lacking the previous friendly and easy buttons for things like input source, numbers and others. And the use of the buttons that do exist is confusing and cryptic, for example, there is no mute button; the mute function is accessed by clicking the volume button straight down, which I only discovered by googling for "no mute button". We won’t even try to give the remote to our guests because it’s unusable without giving them instructions and ongoing tech support to be able to use it. 

And don't buy this TV if you want to watch local channels with an antenna, because the over-the-air channels are buried among the many "smart" screens and menus, again making it almost unusable for guests, and again, because the remote doesn't have an "input source" button that would make it easy.

On the plus side, the quality picture is amazing, especially in 4K.

title: Big Disappointment!
body:
We've exclusively bought Samsung TV's over the years, many of them, and they've been great, until this one. 

The first problem is the power cord socket on the back is stupidly covered by the wall mount bracket, making installation complicated and difficult, and in our case, wasn't even possible with the included power cord, so we couldn't mount it till we found another power cord that would fit. 

The next problem is the TV is much more complicated, made worse by the new remote which is terrible, lacking the previous friendly and easy buttons for things like input source, numbers and others. And the use of the buttons that do exist is confusing and cryptic, for example, there is no mute button; the mute function is accessed by clicking the volume button straight down, which I only discovered by googling for "no mute button". We won’t even try to give the remote to our guests because it’s unusable without giving them instructions and ongoing tech support to be able to use it. 

And don't buy this TV if you want to watch local channels with an antenna, because the over-the-air channels are buried among the many "smart" screens and menus, again making it almost unusable for guests, and again, because the remote doesn't have an "input source" button that would make it easy.

On the plus side, the quality picture is amazing, especially in 4K.

Colors feel rich without looking oversaturated.
For gaming, it supports up to 144Hz with variable refresh rate, and I can genuinely tell the difference, fast action stays smooth with no noticeable tearing. There’s a Gaming portal on the home screen for quick access to game settings, and the interface overall is snappy, with smart apps loading fast.
One note: the built-in speakers are just okay, so if you’re serious about gaming or movie audio, plan on a soundbar. Not a dealbreaker, just something to know going in.
Setup was easy, and this has become the centerpiece of my gaming room.

title: Crisp Viewing Experience
body:
Who needs to go to the movies when you have this TV?! The size is excellent for viewing anything. At close to 150 pounds, it is a lot heavier than my 65in LG tv and it’ll definitely take two people to mount to the wall.  Prior to mounting, I installed the legs to watch a playoff game and the legs are sturdy and easy to attach (no screws needed!).  
The remote is definitely an upgrade and is responsive to when I point, click, or press. The remote has all the necessary options easily accessible, with common apps right on the remote.  
The picture is as crisp as you can get. Anything 4K or animated is clean and detailed. I’ve watched sports, cartoons, and regular shows and they all look excellent. You can customize your picture settings or use the preset ones (standard, vivid, gaming, etc). I switch based on what I’m watching. The picture is fluid with no motion blur, even while gaming.  Since it’s a mini-LED, I don’t expect any burn in, which is nice. I expect to have this TV for a long time with no issues.  
The sound is amazing, even with a ceiling fan on high and the volume on 25/100.  I can see the light reflected from the ceiling fan on the TV but that’s the only glare I can see other than the programming. 
The TV links to the app seamlessly for control without the remote control. The pre-installed apps work just as well as the ones I run from my device.  All in all, a great purchase thus far.
