title: TV's Operating System is Dysfunctional
body:
I am well qualified to judge LG's webOS TV software. My career includes: Business Systems Analyst, Computer Systems Analyst and Method Procedures Analyst. My career also includes 7 years with an aerospace company in Los Angeles. I also owned my own PC and network integration services & support company. 
.
I am not a gamer or graphics developer, and therefore don’t care about ultimate picture quality. Today’s average picture quality is acceptable to me as I just watch basic TV programs and DVDs. Therefore, my critique of LG’s webOS TV operating system and the TV’s functionality are my only focus. My conclusions are supported by my actual user experiences listed below:
.
CONCLUSION: 
============= 
The LG software fails at so many quality control levels. 
The LG TV software has not been quality control tested. 
The LG TV software has not been put through any user ability testing for user perspective feedback 
The technical team does not understand anything from outside of their technical specifications & development. 
.
HERE ARE MY FINDINGS/EXPERIENCES
 = = = = = = = = = = = = = = = = = == = = 
Flawed Setup Routine During First Power on Experience 
--------------------------------------------------------------
First up, when you turn on the TV, it steps you through a very lengthy setup procedure. That's fine if it worked properly. 
My first LG TV (32-in) took me 2 hours to set up. Yes, really! I timed it. Most of the time, it did not accept my remote's button press to navigate and select an option: long press, short press, hard press, soft press. I kept doing those until it finally accepted one of my button presses. It appeared as if the OS setup procedure was too busy doing something behind the scenes to accept my button press.
.
My second (the 43-in LG 43QNED75BUA) LG TV took me only 45 minutes to set up. It was basically the same setup procedure as my other 32-in LG TV, only this time the setup procedure was more responsive to my button press on the remote. I videoed this second set up procedure, which included my voice commentary as things progressed. 
.
Power On The TV 
-----------------------
When powering the TV back on, it is supposed to return you to the channel you last watched. Instead it brings me to the LG app thumbnail screen that contains a little square playing the program where I left off. That's not the same as my 32 inch LG TV which will bring up to a full screen display of the program where I left off. I did change the setting on this TV to do that. However, putting a little preview square amongst the apps, to preview the channel where I left off is not the same as a full screen display of the TV program. I don't want to see your LG apps. I want the full screen display of the channel where I had left off. If I want to see the LG app widgets, I will call for them. Don't force them in my face! 
.
Software Update Changed Some of My Previous Custom Settings 
------------------------------------------------------------------------ 
After running the Wi-Fi software update, some settings got reset back to their original default, after I had previously changed them. 
.
Remote’s Button Press Does NOT Always Work 
---------------------------------------------------------------
Sometimes, when powering on the TV, pressing buttons on the remote doesn't always work. Pressing them hard or pressing them softly doesn't work. Pressing them repeatedly doesn't work. Today I tried to go to channel 4-2 from the original (power on) app display screen, the numbers I pressed were not taking. I got my other LG (identical) remote from my 32-in LG TV that I bought at the same time. There was also no TV response to any button that I pressed on that remote either. 
.
Audio Lags Video 
------------------------
After watching the TV for awhile on LG's Guide channel 261, the audio ends up preceding the video by up to 2-3 seconds. Extremely annoying! There was a setting to synchronize the two. The original default setting of 0 was no longer effective. When I adjusted the setting to increase the number, the video lagged further behind the audio. So a setting of zero was as good as it was going to get. Watching another channel for a while and then coming back to channel 261, the audio and video had resynchronized. But later, the audio and video would get out of sync again. And then on some days, they would not get out of sync and everything would stay okay. WHY??? Don’t blame it on my Wi-Fi or network. As a network technician, the problem is with the TV, not my network. My Roku has no problems. 
.
Sound Stabilization 
--------------------------
There was a setting that would allow for sound volume to remain stable when a louder commercial came on or when changing from one viewing channel to another viewing channel. That does not work. Extremely annoying! 
.
Thumbnail Picture’s Sound 
------------------------------------
While watching a program and I bring up the LG guide, the current channel list displays, with a thumbnail preview box of the channel I was watching. The sound volume gets diminished instead of remaining at the same level it was when I was watching full screen. When I switch back to that same TV channel that's in the thumbnail, the sound volume remains diminished. I have to adjust it upwards back to my normal listening level. 
.
Guide Display 
-------------------
When scrolling through the LG guide, the text for the program's title at the bottom of the screen’s grid is not visible, but the channel’s name and number is visible. When I page down once to scroll the guide, that line at the bottom of the screen does not become the first line at the top of the display guide. The guide scrolls past that previously partially displayed line. So you can never see the program title for that line, unless you scroll one line at a time instead of a full page. When I use the Page-Up or Page-Down button to scroll through the guide, it bypasses about 10 channels in the guide. You need to scroll one line at a time to see all of the lines in the channel guide.
.
Channel Guide’s First Point of Focus 
------------------------------------------------
When bringing up the LG channel guide, what is highlighted is the channel name and its number, not the program's name that is in the current time slot that you are watching. That forces me to scroll over (to the right) into the program information area. I have no need for the channel name and number to be highlighted, instead of the program name that I'm currently watching. That's an extra step I have to go through. 
.
More LG Guide Dysfunction 
-------------------------------------
When in the LG guide, and I highlight a program in the current time slot, there is a little box with the letter "i" (to the right of the program name) to get program information. If you select that information box, you get the same information that is displayed at the top of the screen when in the guide. So that information square is superfluous or redundant. It's an unnecessary stop when I'm trying to scroll towards the right to see future programs. It is nuisance value. When selecting that information box, it does give me an option to watch that. That is redundant to just selecting the program name within the guide. 
.
LG Channel Guide Should Not Time Out 
-----------------------------------------------------
While viewing the guide, and I turn my attention to something else, the guide display will time out and return me to the program I was previously watching. So when I go back into the guide to continue from where I left off, I have to start all over again, because when I go back into the guide it brings me to the point of the current program I'm watching, not the previous channel number within the guide whose guide information I was previously viewing. The guide should not time out. If I want to go back to my program, I will close out the guide. It should simply wait for the next user input. There is absolutely no purpose for LG to time out the channel guide, from a user standpoint. 
.
Size of TV Remote is Ridiculously Tiny 
----------------------------------------------------
The remote itself is too tiny to effectively manipulate or to press the desired buttons. If you have man hands, your hands are too big to manage the buttons on the remote. If you have women sized hands, the same dysfunction applies. However if you have infants hands, that's the right size hand to effectively manipulate the remote. However, an infant doesn't know how to watch TV anyway. Such a tiny-tiny remote is extremely dysfunctional and is extremely not user friendly. There have been numerous complaints about that. LG saved a dollar and could care less about their customer’s usability! Because LG chose to make the remote as tiny as possible, obviously to save money, again I say that the remote is extremely dysfunctional. The buttons are too close together, are too tiny and the user many times accidentally presses the wrong button. 
.
More Remote Dysfunction 
------------------------------------
The remote is extremely useless when viewing the TV at night in a dimly lit room or with the lights out. Because there is no backlight glow on the remote, you can't see the button's icons. 
.
Magic Remote
--------------------
LG Talks about getting their Magic Motion Remote Control (Model = MR26GA) and how much better/easier it is to use than their regular infant-sized remote control. I went to LG's web site and there are no search results for that model number. I wen to the Best Buy store where I bought my 2 LG TVs and spoke with the LG rep about that. I was told that LG is not making the Magic Motion Remote. He then pointed me to generic magic remotes that the store had. HELP ME LG! How do I get an LG Magic Motion Remote???

LG: Please Email me. There is more, but there is a review size limit.

title: Great tv—but no Magic Remote is a serious issue.
body:
Just bought this tv yesterday and it is, in fact, fantastic. However, as others have pointed out, there's no Magic Remote. I'm not just disappointed, I'm actually concerned that this borders on misleading advertising: ALL the marketing material focuses on AI functions WITH the Magic Remote. Unlike added functionalities available with an LG soundbar, there is no asterisk warning that the remote isn't included on the model I purchased (65in). The standard remote is listed in the specs, but that's far too easy to miss when you've just been bombarded by images of the Magic Remote as a main selling point. 

So, I now own a television that effectively locks me out of most of its touted, standout features. For me (and others who bought this tv based on ad copy), all the promotional videos on this page, and on the store's web page where I made the purchase, are simply not true. In fact, I can't even find this remote model listed anywhere. I read the reply about the Magic Remote being available to "further enhance" the experience but, with all due respect, that's not how you present it. At all. The promotional material even says "your Magic Remote" not "a Magic Remote". That doesn't sound like an add-on.

As I said: the UA77 is a wonderful television. It really is. I would've given it 4 stars, easily. But I'm just profoundly disappointed with LG. This isn't right.

title: great picture, terrible user interface
body:
Two stars only because the clarity is very good.  The TV picture is great.  However, the user interface running the device is terrible.  It barely responds to the remote control.  Instead of a button in the center of the directional arrows, there is a scroll wheel.  But the scroll wheel does not do what you expect it to do, instead of moving from icon to icon, it activates a remote pointer mouse.  Well the pointer mouses accuracy is horrendous.  It jumps all over the screen, it clicks where you don't want it to, and doesn't click where you want it to.

My recommendation for you before buying any television is to get the remote from sales and operate the tv, not just watch the high-resolution picture on display.  This tv is very difficult to navigate. And there is no place to disable this annoying feature. 

Also, do not be fooled by the AI tag, this is NOT AI.  The help feature they call chatbot, does not give prompts, it is merely a pre-defined set of questions and answers.  Maybe they have some AI running in the background recording all you do so it can present content you are interested in, but even that is NOT AI, but simply maching learning and recording. 

don't be fooled, get the remote from sales, operate the TV.  Make sure you are good with how this works.

Also, the chromecast and apple air play barely work.  I was finally able to use them both, but it seems to hang on to the connection after disconnection, so a second user cannot also cast via apple.  The response time is slow and laggy when it finally does connect.

title: Great tv—but no Magic Remote is a serious issue.
body:
Just bought this tv yesterday and it is, in fact, fantastic. However, as others have pointed out, there's no Magic Remote. I'm not just disappointed, I'm actually concerned that this borders on misleading advertising: ALL the marketing material focuses on AI functions WITH the Magic Remote. Unlike added functionalities available with an LG soundbar, there is no asterisk warning that the remote isn't included on the model I purchased (65in). The standard remote is listed in the specs, but that's far too easy to miss when you've just been bombarded by images of the Magic Remote as a main selling point. 

So, I now own a television that effectively locks me out of most of its touted, standout features. For me (and others who bought this tv based on ad copy), all the promotional videos on this page, and on the store's web page where I made the purchase, are simply not true. In fact, I can't even find this remote model listed anywhere. I read the reply about the Magic Remote being available to "further enhance" the experience but, with all due respect, that's not how you present it. At all. The promotional material even says "your Magic Remote" not "a Magic Remote". That doesn't sound like an add-on.

As I said: the UA77 is a wonderful television. It really is. I would've given it 4 stars, easily. But I'm just profoundly disappointed with LG. This isn't right.

title: Great TV, Auracast does not work unfortunately
body:
This is a review for the LG OLED83B5 series TV.  This television has a wonderful picture and when paired up with an external speaker or sound bar, leads to an exceptional entertainment experience.  My wife loves the tv.  I however, do have some complaints involving the new Auracast broadcast, as to which I’m hoping will be resolved in a future software update.  For those of us who have hearing aids, Auracast will transmit the tv audio directly to your hearing aids phone app using Bluetooth technology.  Unfortunately on this tv, after pairing the Auracast broadcast to my Jabra hearing aids app (EnhancePro),  the tv remote functionality seized up, leaving on/off as the only button that worked.   I tried turning it off & on, unplugging it, I even did a factory reset, but when I tried connecting to the Auracast broadcast, the tv froze up.  There were some trial periods when the tv worked briefly but seized up again after stopping a video.   I’m guessing that it’s a Bluetooth bug that hopefully can be resolved with a software fix.  

Another issue with Auracast on this tv is that there is no USER audio modulation adjustment.  The audio transmission output is too high for my comfort level….I had to turn my hearing aid app’s adjustment all the way down and it still felt too loud for my comfort! 

Why is there NO user manual for this particular model on the LG website?  You can download the quick setup guide and safety guide but no full user manual!

body:

Purchased this model, because of not needing a sound bar.  Not interested in gaming, but wanted a tv for watching tv: live sports, tv shows and streaming, movies on DVDs and sports.  After a week or 2 of picture and sound adjustments, I think I got the settings just right, but can't quite get the viewing of hockey adjusted,  The whites from the ice and jerseys are off and the sound is tinning for some reason.  

One piece of advice if you buy one: don't just click "accept all" when you're setting it up. Take time to look through the privacy settings and terms. There’s a lot of bloatware and ad banners that can make the home screen very cluttered, so it's definitely worth the effort to turn that off.

Movies look amazing on it, especially with the deep blacks from the OLED screen. Dark scenes actually have detail instead of looking gray or washed out, and the colors pop in a way that makes the whole picture feel more realistic. You can also really notice the pixel quality up close. The image stays sharp and smooth, whether I’m watching something cinematic or just regular TV.

It’s also been great for sports, especially watching games like the NBA Finals. The motion looks smooth, the court colors look vibrant, and the picture is clear enough that it makes the game feel more immersive. The 65 inch size gives it that theater feel without being too much for a living room, and the viewing angles are really nice too. Even from the side, the picture still looks great. Overall, it’s a beautiful TV with great color, sharp pixels, deep contrast, and a viewing experience that makes everything from movies to basketball feel way more enjoyable.

title: Spectacular OLED TV
body:
The 65-inch LG C6 OLED is an outstanding TV, with perfect blacks, great brightness and overall amazing picture quality. If you are coming from an older TV, especially a non-OLED model, the difference is absolutely night and day.

The built-in speakers are surprisingly good, especially with AI Sound Pro turned on. The HDR performance, pixel brightness, picture modes and high refresh rate make this TV feel very premium. Built-in cloud gaming also works amazingly well, almost as if you are using a console. Using a PS5 with this TV is another level, with HDR making games look bright, colourful and very immersive.

WebOS is also surprisingly good compared to other built-in TV operating systems I have used. The picture quality is stunning across everything, from live TV to Netflix, YouTube and Apple TV+.

Assembly was straightforward with two people and a Phillips head screwdriver. The slimness of the TV really stands out, as the panel is incredibly thin. The stand also looks sleek, luxurious and sits at a great height.

The built-in OLED care features and automatic pixel cleaning are great to have and give extra peace of mind for long-term use. The only thing I wish this TV had was a gigabit Ethernet port, as streaming apps and cloud gaming could benefit from faster wired speeds, although I understand most OLED TVs still use standard Ethernet ports.

Overall, this TV is a true all-rounder. If you are considering it, I would definitely recommend going ahead with the purchase.

title: Great panel, horrid support and arc issues
body:
Let me start by saying this is my 4th OLED TV,  ALL LG. The picture is amazing, and plenty bright. Colors look accurate for my product photos and gaming feels great. Truly one of the best looking displays.

Now, onto all the issues. First off, the #1 reason I even upgraded to this model from the CX 77 was because that TV had an arc issue no matter what. Sometimes the speakers would work, yet most of the time we had to a hard reset on the receiver just to get them to link up again and output sound. So, I got the CX fixed(new motherboard) and same issue. I even got a new receiver, same issue. Clearly a software issue. So got sick if it and got the G5 83 in hopes that the new software, and tech would fix it. NOPE. Same exact issue, right off that bat. Trying to fix for months and not one thing works to fix it. And now I can't even get sound after hard reset. After trying to get past LGs AI bots for weeks, I finally got a tech here, since that is all they want to do. Same guy as before from years ago. He said it is a common known issue with LG and is likely the software. He mentioned some receivers play nicer than others(even though I read about LG's own soundbar having the same issue.) So he could do nothing but replace the motherboard, and he said there was no point as the ports function fine and is a software issue. LG will not do anything, the just want to send ANOTHER tech. Been dealing with this for months. We should either get a refund, recommended receiver, or the new model. This whole experience has been bad after dropping $4,500...

Other mentions. The software is so slow, and is filled with advertisements, and ai learning, which I keep choosing to opt out of. IT COMES BACK. The controller is joke but no mute button, no hdmi buttons, no picture mode switch button, no backlight. There are a good amount of apps, but it is painfully slow to use. 

In the end, this is a case of a truly great panel, that is destroyed with bad software and even worse support. I don't think I would buy another LG product after this. They don't have our backs,  just our wallets.

The design is another highlight. It looks sleek, modern and premium, and despite the huge screen it has an elegant appearance that fits beautifully into the room. The smart TV interface is quick and easy to navigate, and everything feels polished and responsive.

What impresses me most is just how much of an upgrade the G5 feels every time I switch it on. Even after owning it for a while, I still find myself appreciating the picture quality. HDR content in particular can look absolutely breathtaking.

If you’re looking for a premium large-screen OLED and want exceptional picture quality, performance and design, I can wholeheartedly recommend the LG G5 77". It’s an outstanding television and easily one of the best technology purchases I’ve made.

For webOS it's the small things like an unintuitive home screen, not being able to change the screen saver, and all the unnecessary bloat that really leave me scratching my head. WebOS is like Windows Mobile was for smart phones - built by people who don't have the slightest clue what consumers want.

title: Absolute Masterclass in Picture Quality and Design
body:

​Moving to the OLED65G64LW has been an absolute revelation. The jump from 55 to 65 inches is impressive on its own, but the sheer leap in technology over the last ten years is mind-blowing.
​The brightness levels on this G-series panel are a massive step up from my old B6—it handles room reflections effortlessly while keeping those famous, perfect OLED blacks. Knowing how much LG has advanced their built-in panel-care features, logo luminance adjustment, and anti-burn-in tech over the years gives me massive peace of mind this time around, especially for broadcast TV and subtitles.
​The design is a work of art it mounts incredibly flush to the wall, looking completely seamless and premium. The smart webOS interface is also lightning-fast compared to older generations.
​If you are hesitating to upgrade an older OLED, don't look back. This is a masterful piece of engineering and proves why LG still leads the way.

title: LG G5 77" OLED – My Owner Review
body:
[This review was collected as part of a promotion.] I have recplaced my 14 year old Sony TV with LG G5 77" one. 

Buying the LG OLED evo G5 77-inch has genuinely been one of the best decisions I’ve made when it comes to home entertainment.

From the very first movie and sports stream, the TV felt fun, cinematic, and deeply immersive in a way that instantly justifies the upgrade. The 77-inch screen size creates a true theatre-like presence in the room, and paired with OLED’s perfect contrast, it transforms every piece of content into an event.

The brightness is exceptional, especially for an OLED. HDR highlights have real punch, specular details pop beautifully, and daytime viewing is no longer a compromise. Even in a brighter room, the picture remains vibrant and impactful without losing the OLED magic.

Where this TV really shines is in its black levels and contrast. Blacks are truly inky and absolute, making dark scenes look rich and dimensional rather than washed out. The depth this adds to films, especially sci-fi, thrillers, and Dolby Vision content, is stunning. Shadow detail remains excellent while still preserving that infinite contrast OLED is famous for.

Motion performance is another standout. Sports look incredibly smooth, fast camera pans remain controlled, and action scenes in movies feel natural without excessive artefacts. The motion handling strikes a fantastic balance between clarity and cinematic presentation, which makes both live sports and blockbuster films equally enjoyable.

Colour reproduction is also superb. Skin tones look natural, vibrant scenes have incredible richness, and the panel’s overall accuracy makes premium streaming content look spectacular. Combined with the size and brightness, the picture often feels almost three-dimensional.

Most importantly, this TV makes watching content genuinely fun again. Whether it’s movies, sports, OTT streaming, or casual YouTube sessions, the experience feels premium, immersive, and special every single time.

Its worth even more when it is sold a a discounted price compared to the launch price. In my opinion, the LG G5 77" is easily one of the best TVs available today, and I’m extremely happy with the decision.

## LG G3 77" OLED – My Review

I’ve been using the 77" LG G3 for a while, and the picture quality is honestly the standout. The blacks are perfect as you’d expect from OLED, but what impressed me most is how bright it gets — HDR content really pops and looks incredibly detailed.

The design is super thin and looks amazing on the wall, though it’s clearly built more for mounting than using on a stand. For everyday viewing, everything looks sharp, and even older content holds up well.

Gaming has been great too — smooth, responsive, and no noticeable lag.

The sound is just okay, so I’d recommend a soundbar. It’s also quite expensive, and I’ve noticed slight dimming in very bright scenes.

Overall, I’m really happy with it — if you want top-tier picture quality, it’s definitely worth considering.

title: Just Wow
body:
[This review was collected as part of a promotion.] I’ve owned a lot of TVs over the years, but the LG OLED77G54LW is on another level entirely. From the moment it powered on, the picture quality was genuinely jaw-dropping. The contrast is what really sets it apart. Watching films on this feels like having a private cinema at home. Dolby Vision content looks stunning, with incredible detail in both dark scenes and bright ones. You start noticing things in movies you’ve watched for years that you never saw before.

Gaming has also been phenomenal. With the near-instant response time and smooth motion, everything feels incredibly fluid. Fast scenes remain razor sharp and immersive.

What surprised me most was the viewing angles. Even when sitting off to the side, the colours and contrast stay consistent. That makes a big difference in a family living room where everyone isn’t sitting directly in front of the screen.

The design is also beautiful. Mounted on the wall it looks more like a piece of art than a television. The slim gallery design makes it blend into the room perfectly.

But the real magic is the sense of immersion. The combination of deep contrast, brilliant brightness, and massive 77-inch screen pulls you right into whatever you’re watching.

Honestly, this is the first TV I’ve owned where guests walk into the room and immediately say “wow”. If you want a television that genuinely feels like a generational leap in picture quality, this is it.

title: Stunning picture, frustrating software
body:
[This review was collected as part of a promotion.] The image quality is fantastic and exactly what I expected. Bright, sharp, and genuinely impressive.

Unfortunately the software experience lets it down. webOS feels limiting compared with a proper Google TV setup. I cannot install native Google TV or Android TV friendly apps, so I am forced to stick to whatever is available in the webOS app catalogue.

Bluetooth audio is also fiddly. If I use an external Bluetooth speaker, after powering the TV off and back on the speaker often needs reconnecting again, which gets annoying fast.

The remote is another disappointment. It has lots of shortcut buttons for apps I do not use and I find that inconvenient. Other brands offer remotes without these shortcuts, and at this price I expected more premium attention to detail.

There are also missing quality of life features that are standard on Google TV, like automatically launching a chosen app after power on.

Finally, I do not use cable, aerial or satellite input at all, so I do not need channel tuning or TV related menus, yet there is no option to disable that side of the interface and hide it properly.

Overall, an excellent panel held back by the platform and small but constant annoyances.

title: Nearly Perfect.
body:
The LG 83” G5 is a stunning TV and easily one of the best displays I’ve owned. The picture quality is phenomenal—deep blacks, excellent contrast, and a clean, vibrant image that looks fantastic no matter what I’m watching. Everything feels quick and responsive, and after a couple of weeks of daily use, the performance has been consistently excellent. From a pure viewing standpoint, this TV absolutely delivers.

Where it falls short is in the gallery experience, which was a major reason I chose this model. During my research, I reviewed what appeared to be the gallery functionality for this TV, but after purchase I realized much of that content reflected the previous version of LG’s Gallery rather than the current Gallery Plus. The current implementation is more limited and seems to remove support for truly static images and other features that previously existed. I haven’t found a way to restore the older version, which was disappointing.

Customization options could also be improved. More control over gallery behavior and system settings would better match the premium nature of the TV and elevate the overall experience.

Overall, the LG 83” G5 offers incredible picture quality and strong performance, and I’m very happy with it as a TV. With improvements to the gallery software and deeper customization options, it could easily be a five-star product.

A promotion of a $500 gift card for an LG G5 83" TV purchased between 11/25 and 12/6 is not being honored.  The link is now down: https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSc5FuykFZvSRkNk1o2zuGJpT7-HzupSh6VEqsirk8yAvdSQ5A/closedform?pli=1
There was nothing in the terms and conditions that stated any kind of limitation on the promotion.  A chat with LG support tells me: "We really appreciate your interest in our review campaign! The response was incredible, and all gift cards have already been claimed, which is why the campaign ended earlier than expected. We truly appreciate your enthusiasm and support, and we look forward to sharing more exciting opportunities with you soon."
How would I have known there's a limit to the gift cards?  It's so time consuming to deal with support.  The promotions phone# 833 558 2155 just rings to a busy signal every time (maybe because of this).  It's also very time consuming to deal with a return.  I've already had the tv mounted on my wall.  Maybe that's what LG is counting on?  Scam people in such a way that they give up, and we dont have to pay for the promotion we advertised.

title: Best OLED on the market!
body:
The LG G5 OLED is an incredible TV. It has perfect blacks along with the brightness of an LED. This is hands down the best OLED on the market. I have previously owned three different version of the LG C series TVs, and this has by far the best picture quality (Dolby Vision), higher refresh rate for gamers and all of the built in apps you could want. The preset picture modes are great, and one new cool feature is you can customize your own picture mode based on your personal preferences, which is a good addition. The upgraded brightness and sleek wall design of the G series compared to the C series is definitely worth it if you’re a tv enthusiast. 

The only con (besides the higher price point) is the remote control doesn’t work as well as prior models, but can still get by. You can also connect an Xbox controller directly to the TV through Bluetooth which is a cool wow factor and play games directly through the TV via cloud gaming. Overall am very happy with the TV and would recommend it! The built in tv speakers are pretty good for a tv, but would highly recommend getting a compatible Dolby Atmos capable soundbar as well to take advantage of the best quality sound available.

title: Early Impressions of the "Best" TV in Existence
body:
I recently upgraded to the 83” LG OLED, and so far it’s been impressive. The picture quality really delivers with deep blacks, immensely bright visuals, and sharp detail, especially in HDR. Soccer and Movies look fantastic at this size, and the ultra-thin profile gives it a premium feel on the wall.

There are a few early drawbacks, though. WebOS still isn’t great—it’s functional, but not as streamlined or intuitive as the ROKU interface for example. I also had some difficulty getting it to play nicely with my Sonos sound system, which took more tinkering than expected. And while it mounts fairly close to the wall, it’s not as completely flush as something like The Frame TV. If you’re hoping to add a decorative frame, be aware there aren’t really off-market frame options available for a screen this size/model.

All that said, these are early impressions. I’ve only had limited time with it, and I’m still testing different content, calibration settings, and integrations. Based on initial use, it’s a fantastic display and a big upgrade—just not a totally seamless ecosystem experience. I’ll update once I’ve spent more time with it.

title: Can't go wrong with OLED, 4 stars due to issues
body:
TV itself is great. Filmmaker mode looks odd, so would need to switch to Cinema mode for "old" Filmmaker functionality that I saw in my 77inch CX model. Sound quality is great, better than expected coming from the TV itself. The UI in the CX is much better than what is available in the G5: the screensaver pushes ads constantly, if you let the TV idle, it'll play ads. I still need to mess around with the settings to see how I can disable these ads or if it's even possible to disable them in the first place. 

Much brighter than the CX. The one feature so far that I've noticed does not work is the Screen Share for laptops/PCs. Maybe this can be fixed in the future with a software update but as of now, I can only mirror my phone using Google Cast but sharing PC screen does not work as it did in the CX.

The magic remote that came with the CX is miles better than the one that comes with the G5. There is no dedicated mute button so you have to sit there with your thumb on the volume until it goes all the way down. The cursor movement is controlled by the "enter" button as was in the CX remote but it seems much easier to accidentally enable the cursor when you're trying to press enter with this new remote.

Overall, the experience and picture quality has been great so far. I'm hoping that some of the issues that I've experienced can be remedied by messing with the settings, waiting for a future software update, and possibly buying a different remote that is compatible with the G5.

title: LG 85” G5 Great Product
body:
This Tv leaves little to be desired. I’ve recently upgraded from LG’s Nanocell 75” (which also was a great product) and the difference is stark. The colors are deep and rich, the UI is snappy, clarity is unreal. But there are a few things that I would like to see improved. The remote feels like a slight downgrade from its predecessor, with the removal of the input button, and the voice assistant is sometimes difficult to use. The “Hey LG” feature stops listening as soon as you finish the acknowledgement and doesn’t proceed with your request. The remote assistance is much more smooth. Some of the settings are hard to find/ navigate as there’s 3 menus to sift through (primary settings, alternative settings, and game mode settings that only show up when the Tv recognizes a console or PC. 

As far as the panel goes, this TV is superb, I had a concern for brightness moving from my last tv which had several glares throughout the day but this TV has no issue overpowering them. The antiglare finish diffuses ambient light exceptionally. And brightness is a concern of the past. I’ve found myself on several occasions squinting or turning the brightness down just to make the screen tolerable to look at without adjusting my eyes. You can see reflections off the faces of viewers in a nighttime setting. Rewatching HDR 4K content is like watching for the first time. You can clearly see individual strands of hair, veins on the leafs in the background, the differentiation of colors is otherworldly. 

I wasn’t sure how much of an issue it would be to not have DTS pass through when I purchased, and it still hasn’t been a huge problem, but there is some content out there that uses DTS and not being able to pass the audio through to a receiver when still using the video has proven to be less than ideal for a TV at this price point. Still, the Deal that LG offers for bundling this TV, paired with discounts and deals is superb. I don’t see myself wanting an upgrade for many years to come

Gaming? Forget it. The PS5 on this TV is stupid good. Zero lag, everything feels buttery smooth, and the size just pulls you into the game. It’s honestly a little addicting.

The design is another big win. Since it sits flat against the wall, it doesn’t make my place feel cluttered. That mattered a lot for a studio — it actually makes the room look bigger, not smaller.

Sound is okay, but I added a soundbar because if you’re going this big, you might as well go all in.

If you’re in a small apartment and debating whether an 83-inch TV is “too much,” trust me — it’s not. It’s the best kind of overkill.

title: Amazing Size, Older Panel Tech
body:
The 97-inch LG G5 is an incredible TV in sheer size and picture presence, but it’s important to know what you’re actually getting. Unlike the smaller G5 models, the 97-inch version does not use LG’s new four-stack/tandem OLED panel. Just like past years, the 97-inch models also skip MLA.

From what I understand, it comes down to the way OLED panels are cut from a mother glass sheet. A 97-inch panel uses almost the entire sheet by itself, so LG can’t divide it into multiple panels like they do with smaller sizes. Since this size is already extremely expensive, adding the newest and most expensive panel tech might push the price even higher than it already is.

So while the TV still delivers excellent OLED picture quality, you should know you’re not getting the latest generation panel advancements. If you’re buying specifically for the cutting-edge tech, this is something to keep in mind. If you’re buying for size and immersion, it’s unmatched.

title: The King of OLED TVs
body:
The LG OLED83G5WUA isn’t just a TV — it’s a centerpiece. From the moment you turn it on, you’re met with a picture so rich and immersive it almost feels three-dimensional. LG’s OLED evo technology, paired with the new Alpha 11 AI Processor, takes everything you watch and elevates it — whether it’s a 4K HDR film or a 1080p stream. The clarity, contrast, and color accuracy are truly world-class. Blacks are absolute, highlights pop, and the overall image looks more natural than ever.

What impressed me most is how bright this OLED can get. Traditionally, OLEDs struggled in well-lit rooms, but LG’s Brightness Booster Max and improved heat dissipation make this panel more capable than any OLED before it. Whether you’re watching a game in daylight or a movie at night, the picture remains vibrant and consistent.

For gamers, it’s a dream setup. The 165 Hz refresh rate, HDMI 2.1 ports, NVIDIA G-Sync, and AMD FreeSync Premium support make everything ultra-responsive. There’s virtually no input lag, and motion stays razor-sharp. Add to that the TV’s fast 0.1 ms response time, and you get a competitive edge with stunning visual fidelity.

The design deserves a mention too. LG’s “One Wall Design” lets the screen sit flush against the wall, creating a clean, gallery-style aesthetic. It’s minimalist, modern, and makes even a massive 83-inch panel look elegant rather than overwhelming.

Sound quality is equally refined. With Dolby Atmos and AI sound processing, the built-in speakers produce an unexpectedly full soundstage. Still, pair it with a quality soundbar or receiver and you’ll have a home-theater experience that rivals most cinemas.

There are very few drawbacks here. The price is premium — but so is everything about this TV. And while reflections can still occur in very bright environments, LG has done an excellent job reducing glare compared to past models.

Final Verdict

If you’re looking for the best possible large-screen experience, the LG OLED83G5WUA is it. It delivers jaw-dropping visuals, elite gaming performance, an art-gallery design, and next-gen smart features that make everyday use effortless.

It’s not just one of the best OLED TVs of 2025 — it’s one of the best TVs ever made.

title: Life's Definitely Good with this immersive OLED
body:
[This review was collected as part of a promotion.] There are only a handful of OLED TVs that are classed as the best right now in 2025. I picked this for it's all-rounder ability to do everything great!

Receiving it is a delight but unlike TVs of the past and in smaller sizes, this 77 inch version of the G5 is a heavy and more importantly large TV. No longer can it be setup by one strong person. Once setup it is beautiful! Don't forget to peal of the screen protector. You'll be able to tell from the little red sticker on the bottom right that you can use to peal it off. I was scared that it was a layer on the display but thankfully it's a screen protector that's a life saver when putting grubbing hands on it when standing or mounting.


Pros:

- It may seem like a huge TV and it sure is, but it's one of the most stunning immersive experiences you can have with a TV. I jumped up from a 55 inch and it was a huge difference.
This might sound crazy to some but while the official seating position is around 5-6 metres, i sit 2 metres away, and i would not have it any other way. Sitting 3+ metres away definitely gives you slightly better clarity, but less than 3 metres is definitely the way to go if you want pure immersion to the edges of your eyes.

- The display is stunning, beautiful, soooo bright. No more issues with dim OLEDs which i don't think i ever had, but for my TV i moved from a LED to this OLED. It's going to be many many years before any tech beats the OLED TVs. QNEDs, LEDs, MiniLED, even with their coloured RGB backlights are still not good enough, so you can definitely rest that no tech will beat this TV in at least 5 years on this scale at a consumer price.

- Getting a large TV can have it's issues such as with blowing up non 4K resolutions to 77 inches. I got this because of it's AI upscaling capabilities for SD and HD content. And i can say that regular TV viewing is greatly enhanced for a great large TV experience. This was actually my reason to go for the G5 instead of the C5. They are both equally as beautiful, but if want that extra push in the AI upscaling department that's where this shines.

- Watching movies on this is so much like a mini cinema experience. Grab your popcorn, pizza, or bag Cheetos and you're sorted. I do a lot of Plex streaming to it and i absolutely love it.

- Gaming is absolutely wowzers! It has a great gaming mode and playing games on this is one of the most amazing experiences you'll have. There can be a few difficulties when gaming if your sitting close to the display which i have noted in the cons, but this is a large TV issue and not an issue with this TV.
Setting up consoles for this is a breeze, and you'll notice that every capability of current gen Xbox Series X and PlayStation 5 are usable on this TV - all those 4K HDR ALLM VRR High BIT etc.

- The TV and is WebOS has a lot of features. Once you connect online to a wireless or wired network, you have a whole host of things you can download on it and do. Connectivity to Bluetooth controllers, networks, devices, and app services is simpler than many previous TVs and especially from other brands.

- TruMotion is incredible! Use it where you wish but if you can make yourself adapt to it, it makes almost everything that much more amazing. I know it's blasphemous for many, but there are many secrets of the industry that will make you realise why film was made at 24 fps and not more. Once you peak your curiosity of what film was meant to be from the start, you may want to experiment, and that experimenting may just surprise you, if you can give yourself a couple of weeks to adapt.

Cons:

- As with all TVs, the built-in speakers aren't going to be comparable to external speaker systems, but they do a good job for internal speakers. The various sound modes are great, especially the AI audio enhancement, but don't expect miracles.

- Since this is a Gallery TV, (which basically means it's so big that it's designed for wall mounting like a picture frame) it cannot be put on a stand by default. You can however purchase a universal large TV pedestal stand and mount it onto that and have it standing, and even on a stand it looks beautiful. I purchased a Bontec stand from Amazon.

- Gaming has two issues which are more about large TVs than this TV.
If you sit far away then this first issue is mitigated and that is that the large TV means that when you are playing games that require you to look to the edges of the screen, e.g., minimaps, HUD elements, you'll need to adapt yourself to looking when you can, otherwise you may realise you have to move so far away from the main content because of the large size, that when you look back, you've crashed your car.
BUT every game is an absolutely beauty on these, and even more so when they have features such as HDR.
The second issue is perhaps a bigger one, and that is, due to the large display, playing games at 30 fps caps are much more pronounced, and you feel the judder a lot more. I very rarely play a 30 fps game now on it because it's almost headache inducing for me, but then i am very sensitive to frame rates. The higher the frame rate on this high refresh rate TV the better. And anything 60 fps and higher is stunning!


Conclusion

You cannot go wrong with this TV. The top three TVs on the market are at this level, but the quality, build, features, AI upscaling, TruMotion, and other enhancements with it newer processor are something that made this TV stand out from the rest.

The next thing is to find a sound system that matches it's beautiful picture for the true in-home cinema experience.

Last bit of advice. You can definitely use this TV straight out of the box without doing anything in the settings, but i do recommended it. It can be daunting if you really want to set everything up and don't know where to start. Look for some setup guides and picture calibration guides on YouTube. Found one that was an hour long for the previous model, and using it calibrated the display to an even more stunning experience.

Oh and keep that thing clean. OLEDs can be difficult to clean if you get finger prints on them.

If you want it, buy it, love it, and never look back. Until it's 5 to 10 years time and you want to go to 100 inches!

title: The LG G5 is a total beast!
body:
The LG OLED G5 TV is the flagship consumer model for 2025 and brings the best features and brightest screen available from LG this year. I picked up the 65” model to replace an older 55” OLED from about 9 years ago. If you have not experienced a quality OLED screen before then prepare to be amazed, but I do have experience with them (also have a 77” G1 from a few years ago in another room) and the G5 is still super impressive. Image quality is unmatched by most options in the marketplace and the deep blacks and high brightness is a real treat with HDR content. 

I have this set up primarily for 4K movie playback and  gaming on a PlayStation 5 Pro, which was one of my main reasons for upgrading. I wanted to take advantage of the 4k 120hz display and a larger screen is always nice. 
I also used some built in apps just to confirm Dolby Vision was working, etc. Most likely I will connect a Roku or some dedicated streaming device if I really want to use those services though. 

I knew this model had the flush wall mount option and the installation was an included bonus from buying direct at LG. It looks pretty incredible up on the wall. Very sleek. Once the tv is up on the wall ( which is a bit tricky) you have very limited range of motion or space to maneuver to get hdmi/ethernet cables connected, get the power cord plugged in, etc (also make sure you have a recessed plug if you want the TV flush to the wall), so plan accordingly. 

Before I decided to buy this I did research and was aware of some issues with streaming content with Dolby vision that was apparently addressed with a recent firmware update. I am still messing around with the picture settings and trying to tweak it for the best results but I haven’t noticed any glaring issues yet. There are a lot of picture options but it seems like “filmmaker mode” is the priority for the firmware fixes. Something to keep an eye on as they roll out more updates throughout the life of the TV. 

So far I am still pretty early in the process of getting it all set up, but everything went pretty smooth so far. All of my devices are  connected through my AVR which is connected to the television using 1 hdmi cable in the eArc port (hdmi 2). I don’t use the tv speakers but I did listen to them before setting up the avr and they are adequate. With a tv like this you deserve a soundbar at least, or an actual surround sound speaker setup. 

Hopefully future system updates continue to improve and add features but so far so good with this new TV. I am hoping for many years of use ahead.

title: A Masterpiece of Modern Display Engineering
body:
[This review was collected as part of a promotion.] When you unbox the LG OLED77G54LW, you're not just unveiling a television — you're revealing a centrepiece, a cinematic marvel, and quite possibly the finest piece of display technology available in its class.

From the moment this 77-inch behemoth powers on, it's clear that LG isn’t just playing the game — they’re rewriting the rules. The OLED evo panel in the G5 series has taken a dramatic leap forward in both luminance and refinement. Blacks are, as expected, inky and infinite. But it's the improved peak brightness and HyperReal Colour fidelity that push this set into the stratosphere. HDR content, particularly Dolby Vision, doesn't just pop, it breathes.

Gamers, rejoice. With HDMI 2.1 across all ports, G-SYNC and FreeSync Premium, and VRR at up to 120Hz, this TV isn’t just future-proof, it’s future-dominant. Paired with an ultra-low input lag and LG’s superb Game Optimiser dashboard, the OLED77G54LW is a weapon of choice for next-gen consoles.

Design-wise, the G5 series continues its Gallery tradition: slim, flush-to-wall elegance that turns the TV into a living artwork. It’s stunning when off and jaw-dropping when on.

The webOS experience has been cleaned up this year, offering snappier transitions and smarter recommendations without overstepping and the new α11 AI Processor? It’s the silent genius behind the scenes, ensuring upscaling, motion smoothing, and ambient tone mapping are all buttery-smooth and eerily lifelike.

If there’s a flaw to be found, it's that the OLED77G54LW sets a new bar that few others can reach — including LG's own previous flagships. It's a reminder that OLED technology, when mastered, isn’t just about pixels. It’s about storytelling.

title: LG 77" G5 OLED TV Review
body:

The viewing angles are excellent too — even off-centre, colours and contrast remain intact, making it ideal for wider seating arrangements.

One of the standout features is the anti-reflective coating, which significantly cuts down on glare and reflections, especially in daylight or rooms with ambient lighting. This makes the viewing experience consistently sharp and immersive across varying conditions.

title: Great with a few issues
body:
Overall this is a great TV. The visuals are a 10/10, but there are problems I wish they would fix.

1st problem, no steam link or moonlight support. My gaming PC is in another room, but I can't stream games to the TV. Competition has this feature and it's pretty disappointing WebOS doesn't support it.

2nd problem, eARC audio disconnections. I use a pair of Klipsch the Fives speakers over eARC, but they occasionally disconnect and switch to using the TVs built in speakers. Some days it doesn't disconnect, others I have to switch it back to eARC multiple times. Not a deal breaker, but definitely annoying to deal with while watching a movie.

Neither of these are deal breakers, but with this being an expensive flagship TV it's enough to drop the TV down a star.

Bottom line, if you have a bright room like me this TV is a game changer, as long as these gripes aren't too annoying to you.

But because the tv is so bright even with bfi enabled, the drop in brightness isnt an issue. The brightness of the tv is perfect for bright room viewing.

title: Recommended for anyone with light sensitivity
body: [This review was collected as part of a promotion.] I highly recommend this TV to anyone else who suffers with light sensitivity. Most modern TVs cause me to experience symptoms of eye pain, headache, nausea and dizziness. I wanted an OLED to replace my 2011 plasma, but the first I ordered (the Sony) was unwatchable because of my photosensitivity. I ordered this LG G6 in the hope that the eye care mode (blue light filter) would help. It really does. And interestingly, even with eye care mode turned off, I don't experience the level of symptoms I had watching the Sony OLED. So maybe this type of OLED is better for light sensitive people than QD OLED?  I'm still experimenting with the settings, but the picture out of the box with some minor tweaks is truly amazing. The sound is better than I expected. Having switched off advertising and home screen recommendations, I like the operating system. I think the remote control is rubbish for a premium TV.  Also, I don't want to set up voice command, but if I accidentally press the voice commands button on the remote, the only way to remove the voice command instructions from the screen is to switch the TV off completely. Is there a way to stop this? But otherwise I love my TV.

title: Best TV I've ever watched in any house, anywhere.
body:
This is my favorite TV ever, by a wide margin. It is a remarkable device with amazing performance. Other than a few criticisms, this is the finest TV I've ever watched.

First off, allow me to say how angry I was when I opened the package and there was no stand to which to attach this TV. In my living room where this is placed, wall mounting is not an option; it is resting on an entertainment center. I unboxed this TV and was all set to get right to work, and had to stop in my tracks and rebox it for lack of any means to put up the TV. The LG website and other online listings all showed the dimensions both with and without the stand, and NOTHING I saw or read told me the stand was a separate purchase. So I was forced to spend another unplanned $200 and wait another several days before setting up the TV. Bad first impression, irritated with LG. Nevertheless, now that I have it, the stand  does its job fine. It's a nice low profile and unintrusive. I do not care for the upward tilt, as the TV is already sitting up rather high on an entertainment center. I'm sure there's a stability-related reason for the tilt, but the engineering of the stand should be different so the TV can face straight forward, level. A larger stand profile would not have been a problem.

The setup was easy, no complaints. Self explanatory, simple enough. The Magic remote is neat, very similar to Nintendo Wii. It was my first time with such a remote but it only took me a few seconds to figure out how it worked and begin using it to operate the TV. It also allows for a very clean, simple remote control face, leaving a nice uncluttered layout that I appreciate. I would want to be able to use an older, traditional style of remote, which is available with a readily obtainable universal remote, so no objections here.

The rear of the TV is also very simple and clean. A few HDMI and USB ports, and a small number of miscellaneous ports -- excellent, and with no major limit to function. The eARC/ARC HDMI port is a must-have to enable a premium external audio experience, so I'm glad this critical feature was not overlooked.

Regarding the sound and picture quality -- I actually had a unique and handy advantage in evaluating this TV. My prior TV is an LG 75UH6550, a 75" LG LED HDTV. I therefore was able to directly compare an older LG with older tech to this new set. This helped me really determine with pristine accuracy what is not only good about this new model and tech, but more specifically what has improved over past years and to what degree.

The sound quality is about the same as my 75", and that's a good thing because it's excellent. It's easy to put a garbage or mediocre sound system in a TV because so many novice TV watchers don't understand that sound is a huge part of the viewing experience. LG did not, and still does not, disappoint here. The sound is very good, especially considering how thin the panel now is and how little room there is to put good speakers in there. Job well done. Those who truly care will use an A/V receiver; those who don't care or can't have a receiver will still enjoy a good sound experience. 

The picture quality: wow. Just freaking wow. LG makes an outstanding OLED panel. The contrast is simply the best I've ever seen on any TV, ever. The brightness, how colors look together, how colors pop on the screen, and how blacks are FINALLY BLACK. My 75" LED TV's greatest shortcoming is that blacks were washed out and not distinctive due to backlight bleedthru. This TV, with the ability to shut off a pixel to get complete darkness at the pixel level, is perfect. On movies with black bars, for the first time I can forget the bars are even there, because I can't even see them. Picture detail is so incredibly crisp and fine, I found myself rewinding multiple dark scenes just to appreciate them all over again on this magnificent display.

I have an immense media library, so I was able to view all kinds of content at all kinds of levels. Color and contrast is amazing, both on 4k and 1080p resolutions, as is image detail. At times when image detail was average or poor, it was clear that the TV was not at fault. This display is so good, that it reveals the quality of the video source. The TV was never the limiting factor to a great image, it was always the media that was the bottleneck. Movies that looked poor in 4k -- such as older grainy movies that were upscaled from an HD source (e.g. Air Force One) -- paled in comparison to newer movies that were encoded from a 4k source (e.g. Hunger Games). This panel's 4k ability is remarkable, so I can't blame it when a bad bluray is at fault.

I was able to confirm this by taking high quality 4k blurays and re-encoding them down to 1080p resolution. A good downscaled 1080p encode looked even better than a poor quality 4k bluray. This was solid confirmation that the TV itself was not at fault for poor image quality. I also have many 1080p movies, so I was able to observe many levels of HD quality and see how reveals well this display could reproduce a high quality non-4k image. I tried it with old drawn animation (e.g. Beauty and the Beast), computer generated animation (e.g. Toy Story), and live action (e.g. Airheads). Sometimes it was hard to tell a video source was only 1080p because it looked so good, a true testament to how well this panel works.

I also tried watching some TV series blurays. These typically have much lower bitrates, and it showed. They didn't all look bad, but most did lack the pristine quality of a high bitrate 1080p movie. My 75" LED TV makes the difference between great and mediocre HD source quality much harder to differentiate, meaning it lacks the ability to show a really great 1080p image. This new TV solves that problem in a big way.

In short, this TV is one of the greatest things I own. I've excitedly watched hours and hours of various-quality content on it, and the really good stuff looks REALLY GOOD on it. Sound is very good, picture is freaking excellent, this TV is a big fat winner. I have poker night coming up with some good friends this weekend and I WILL be bragging about this TV. A couple of them are fellow videophiles so I'm sure they'll be interested!

title: Dead On Arrival Flagship Television - AVOID
body:
Please read my story as a warning to others about LG support you may find yourself regretting!  

I purchased this >$5,000 flagship TV directly from LG to avoid any finger pointing issues with delivery damage.  I was in the middle of a new home construction at the time.  It took OVER ONE MONTH for LG to deliver the TV, at which point I had already moved out of my old house and no longer had access to test it when it finally arrived.  Box arrived in flawless condition, so I assumed everything was great!  I stored the TV in a temperature controlled space until the walls were painted.  After an incredibly careful installation - to assure it was perfect - the TV failed to power on.  4 blinking lights as shown in the attached video, indicating a power supply failure.  This TV was completely DOA.  

I called LG support expecting a reasonable outcome, but was instead told they would not replace it!!  I asked to be transferred to their supervisor... and then their supervisor... after pleading with more than 5 more senior people over the course of over 2 hours, I was read the same script repeatedly saying all they can do is send a technician to tear down the TV on the floor of our brand new house and repair it - because it took more than 30 days for me to test it (Ironic, after it took them 40 days to ship it).  This is completely unacceptable to someone who is a perfectionist.  I have my Masters degree in electrical engineering, so please don't brush this off as a consumer-induced problem!  

This may happen to you, and if it does, you will be very sorry you ever purchased a product from LG.  They do NOT stand behind their product and even after escalating to the highest levels of their support staff they are not empowered to do anything to solve your problems except to repeatedly read a script from their screen.    

This was intended to be a centerpiece in the great room of our new house.  Great advertisement for LG, but instead it can only serve as a warning to others.  

I am not an influencer, but I intend to use every available platform to spread my word with the hope that LG will change their ways.  I have been a loyal customer of LG electronics, purchasing tens of thousands of dollars from LG over a 20 year period.  Honestly, I was an unpaid brand ambassador until now.  This was my first support call to them in 20 years (I fixed everything else myself), and you can see how well they took care of me.  Imagine what they will do for you?

title: The Centre Peice My Living Room
body:
(This review was collected as part of a promotion.) The G6 is the premier TV from LG and right out of the box it showed very clearly why. It truly has become the centre piece of my living room and ascends beyond just a TV, it is art. This is my first flagship TV, and out of all my friends and family the only top of the line TV I know of anyone to have. The TV was significantly more affordable than Sony’s offering, and also slightly under the Samsung, however I preferred the glossy look of the LG over the samsungs matte and found the performance the same. We went with the LG and couldn’t be happier. Upon first view the TVs slim frame pops immediately. it looks as if a picture frame itself. The picture quality is so good, that with default settings, certain live sports had become unwatchable, I never realized how poor quality some of these sports broadcast in, and my TV was TOO HD. Luckily the LG has many settings to smooth out the broadcast. I can confidently say the best view of the 2026 FIFA world cup was at my house! The TV has also made watching tv anywhere else a crime, my parents or friends TVs cannot compare to the HD quality and pure blacks the G6 offers, and that would have to be my only complaint. Watching TV on anything other than this TV (or its equals) is sometimes unbearable,  but it’s a downside worth every penny. 

So far as for the reliability, we don’t have any issues as of yet and i’m hoping in the future it can also hold up well.

title: The LG OLED G6 combines incredible 4K picture quality with smart features and an impressive selection of free channels.
body: I’m very happy with the 77 inch LG OLED G6 television. The picture quality is absolutely amazing when watching 4K content. The image is incredibly clear, sharp, and detailed, making movies, sports, and streaming shows look fantastic. The colors are vibrant, and the OLED display really stands out. For non-4K channels, the picture quality is still good, but it is not nearly as crisp as true 4K content. If you watch a lot of 4K programming, this TV really shines. The 77 inch size is perfect for my wall and makes a huge impact in the room without feeling overwhelming. One of the reasons I chose this model was the gallery style design. Initially, we had it wall mounted with the wires visible, and it sat completely flush against the wall. While it looks sleek, the exposed wires took away from the overall appearance. We later had the wires run through the wall, which looks much cleaner and more professional. The trade-off is that the TV no longer sits quite as flush against the wall as it did originally, but the cleaner installation was well worth it. I also love that it’s a smart TV. Setting up and downloading all of my favorite streaming apps was easy, and everything is conveniently accessible in one place. One feature that pleasantly surprised me was the number of free channels included with LG channels. I wasn’t expecting to have access to so much free content right out of the box. There are channels for news, movies, sports, and more, which adds a lot of value without needing additional subscriptions. The included remote is simple, and intuitive, and easy to use. There is a stand available for purchase separately, but we preferred the clean look of a wall mounted installation. Overall, this is an excellent TV outstanding 4K picture quality, a beautiful design, and easy to use smart features. If you’re looking for a premium large screen TV, the LG OLED G6 is a great choice. ￼

title: Premium OLED Performance That Lives Up to the Hype
body:
After spending several weeks with the LG OLED77G6WUA as our primary TV for movies, sports, gaming, and everyday streaming, it's clear this is a premium television that delivers an outstanding overall experience. 
The build quality immediately stands out. The panel feels exceptionally well-made with a slim, premium design that looks fantastic mounted on the wall. Despite its large 77-inch size, it feels sturdy and well-engineered, with excellent fit and finish. Nothing creaks or flexes during installation, giving confidence that it's built to last. 
The included remote is comfortable to hold and intuitive to use, The pointer function makes navigating menus and streaming apps much faster than traditional directional buttons, and voice controls respond accurately for searching content or adjusting settings. Dedicated streaming shortcuts are also a welcome convenience. 
From an ergonomics standpoint, everyday use is effortless. The webOS interface is responsive, inputs switch quickly, and settings are logically organized. Whether adjusting picture modes for movies, enabling Game Optimizer for console gaming, or customizing audio, everything is easy to access. The anti-reflective screen performs well in brighter rooms while still delivering exceptional contrast in darker environments.
After extensive daily use, the TV has remained consistent and reliable. It powers on quickly, maintains a stable Wi-Fi connection, and shows no signs of performance degradation. The premium construction and high-quality materials inspire confidence in its long-term durability. 
Overall, the LG OLED77G6WUA is an exceptional television. Between its premium build, user-friendly remote, thoughtful ergonomics, and dependable performance after extensive testing, it has exceeded expectations and has become the centerpiece of our home entertainment setup. It's a worthwhile investment for anyone looking for a flagship OLED experience.

​The brightness levels on this G-series panel are a massive step up from my old B6—it handles room reflections effortlessly while keeping those famous, perfect OLED blacks. Knowing how much LG has advanced their built-in panel-care features, logo luminance adjustment, and anti-burn-in tech over the years gives me massive peace of mind this time around, especially for broadcast TV and subtitles.
​The design is a work of art it mounts incredibly flush to the wall, looking completely seamless and premium. The smart webOS interface is also lightning-fast compared to older generations.
​If you are hesitating to upgrade an older OLED, don't look back. This is a masterful piece of engineering and proves why LG still leads the way.

title: LG OLED: I understand the hype!
body:
Just moved into my new house and treated myself to this TV and I am genuinely impressed. The picture is amazing.  The blacks are actually black because every pixel lights itself individually, and the brightness is nearly 4 times stronger than older OLEDs.
As a gamer it elevated my whole setup. I didn't realize anything could look this good. 165Hz refresh rate, almost zero response time, and it works seamlessly with both NVIDIA and AMD cards. Smooth doesn't cover it.
I also love that there is a mode that displays films exactly how the director intended. That feature alone is a win for movie nights.

title: Disappointed
body: I’m very disappointed with this product. My G6 has burn-in in under three weeks of owning it. This should not happen with normal viewing. I will buy it from Best Buy or Costco because they will return or exchange it within a reasonable window. I’m so disgusted after spending $4500 plus $200 on a stand to have a TV with burn-in this early. Not to mention the Dolby Vision and motion handling issues this TV has It was not ready to be released obviously, but they released it anyways. title: Very disappointed
body:
I was super excited about this TV with the new panel tech and the brightness boost. Unfortunately, it’s not going very well.  Within a week strange burn in like blotches started to appear on the panel. I noticed it during regular content so I ran a dirty screen test and it was extremely visible. These TVs are supposed to have procedures in place to protect them and burn in under normal viewing should never happen within a week or two of owning. It’s brand new TV. There have also been many other issues that have been addressed by reviewers upon release as well. I’m hoping this bad panel issue. I’m having gets resolved quickly through LG. 

One thing I will say the improved fine detail over the G5 as a huge step up. I will definitely say this TV has potential for incredible image quality and possibly being the best TV of the year as long as there isn’t something actually wrong with the new tandem panel technology, causing people to get early burn in. Right now I’m extremely disappointed after spending $4500 on a TV that should never have issues like this. It’s hard for me to give this anything more than two stars at this point. The only reason it’s getting two stars is because of its potential. Fingers crossed that my panel issues are resolved through LG’s warranty..

title: FINALLY the television that fits our niche needs!
body: Our last TV was 15 years old, stuck out from the wall, and had run its course. We have been moving back toward physical media, DVDs, Blu ray, even VHS, and refused to let that mean downgrading our experience. Think of it like a high end turntable for vinyl. It makes everything you love look better than ever. The picture quality on the LG OLED evo AI G6 is stunning. Watching favorite films on physical media on this screen is something we were not prepared for. The motion smoothing feature called TruMotion can be turned off, giving us back that warm cinematic film look we love. As someone with motion sensitivity and migraines, this was a BIG relief. The Magic Remote with voice search has spoiled us completely. No more typing letter by letter while a toddler screams for their show. The flush wall mount is a dream. Our TV sits near our front door and this one practically disappears against the wall. Review submitted as part of a program that provides a purchase discount.​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​

title: Disappointed at this time
body: I just purchased the G6 after having the G5. I noticed immediately that the G6 is not as bright and many scenes as the G5. This TV is advertised as their brightest OLED ever yet its brightness is not showing. What I will say is it has incredible fine detail and a huge step up in that area over the G5. They’re obviously needs to be some updates because there’s also motion handling issues that are bothering me. The G5 motion handling was perfect after a full year of updates. The G6 has such bad flickering and small, moving objects that they almost disappear, especially movies like Star Wars. My main complaint though is the brightness. I bought this TV because I thought it was going to be a brighter. More vivid TV like it was advertised. It is not at this point. I sincerely hope LG is making effort to fixing this particular issues so that it lives up to the advertising.
